1.name: Josh Allen
1.comment: Allen had another huge season, finishing as the top scoring fantasy quarterback. His passing yards were down a little (3,668) but he had 39 total touchdowns, including 14-rushing scores. Allen also completed a career-best 69.3 percent of his passes. He had the second best on-target percentage (79.9 percent). And he did this with his pass catchers dropping 18 passes, which was the 12th most in football. So his numbers should have been even better throwing the ball. He actually had a great season throwing the ball despite those passing numbers not being quite as good. Some new talent around him this year should help elevate those numbers once again. Allen has 39-plus scores six straight seasons. He is one of the best in the game right now and should be for years to come. He plays in a great offense that caters to his talents. Allen has a huge arm, great size and moves around well for a man of his size. His accuracy has improved a lot since entering the league but he will miss on some throws he probably should make. And his decision making continues to get better, throwing just 16 interceptions his last two seasons. Allen runs very well, posting big rushing numbers on almost a weekly basis. He has double-digit rushing touchdowns three straight seasons.
1.outlook: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen turned in another QB1 finish during the 2025 season, throwing for 3,668 yards, 25 passing touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. On the ground, he enjoyed one of his more productive campaigns, totaling 14 rushing scores (second-most of his career) and adding 579 rushing yards, his most since the 2022 season. This was Allen's third straight season with double-digit rushing touchdowns. Despite his lower passing volume (by passing yardage), ranking 11th among QBs, Allen remains the clear-cut QB1 in all formats given his incredible rushing upside, especially in the red zone. However, there is reason to believe Allen's passing totals could climb in the 2026 season. Last fall, the Bills ran the ball the most times in football, which limited Allen's passing ceiling. While they are unlikely to abandon this game plan as offensive coordinator Joe Brady is set to take over head coaching duties, the acquisition of DJ Moore could raise Allen's passing ceiling. Outside of Khalil Shakir and tight end Dalton Kincaid, Allen did not have many proven options in the passing attack in 2025. Moore had a down season in Chicago in 2025, but still found the end zone six times and has averaged 1,124 yards per season from 2019 through 2024. His elite rushing ability already makes Allen a well-worthwhile selection at his 27.0 ADP on Sleeper (QB1), but there is a clear path for him to return to the 4,000-yard passing floor he showed earlier in his career with Moore leading the wide receiver room. Managers looking to gain a massive edge at the QB position should select Allen with confidence at this cost.

2.name: Lamar Jackson
2.comment: Jackson had arguably the worst season of his career. He missed four games because of injury but was still just 20th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. Jackson had 28-plus fantasy points each of his first three games but didn't reach that mark the rest of the season. He had 20-plus fantasy points just three more games the rest of the year. Jackson had the eighth worst on-target percentage in football (72.4 percent), missing on a lot of throws he normally makes. You have to wonder if nagging injuries were a factor for Jackson throughout the season, especially late in the year. He just didn't look himself, especially when it came to running the ball. He had a career-low 349-rushing yards. Jackson gets a chance to turn it around this year with a new coach and offensive coordinator. Jackson is one of the most dynamic players in the game. Jackson is an elite playmaker as a runner or thrower. He can make plays all over the field because of his athleticism. He lacks a little accuracy throwing the ball but has made big strides in that area since earlier in his career.
2.outlook: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson couldn't overcome early injuries and inconsistency to approach the standard set by his QB1 finish in 2024. The two-time MVP completed 192-of-302 passes for 2,549 yards and a 21:7 TD-to-INT ratio, rushing 67 times for 349 yards and two scores. He suffered a hamstring injury in Week 3 that worsened in Week 4, which led to three games missed. This came after three straight top-four fantasy finishes to open the year. Likely related to this, he later dealt with knee, ankle, and toe injuries, which further limited his mobility. It helps the team when you can hand it off to Derrick Henry rather than risk the QB, but it hurts Jackson's fantasy managers. As a result, he took a career-high sack rate and never had another top-six performance in his other nine games played. However, we still saw a robust 13.3 yards per completion, and the 29-year-old shouldn't carry these injuries into 2026. Our site rank and the market are buying right back in near his ADP of 43, as Jackson remains the second QB off of most draft boards.

3.name: Jayden Daniels
3.comment: After having one of the best seasons ever for a rookie quarterback, Daniels struggled some in year two. He had injury issues but didn't exactly light it up while on the field. He had four of seven games with 20-plus fantasy points. He completed just 60.6 percent of his passes, though, and his season high in passing yards was 233. Daniels just wasn't quite as explosive as he was in year one. He did have some injuries to deal with at receiver and along the offensive line, which didn't help matters for him. Daniels will look to get it going again in year three. He gets a new offensive coordinator, David Blough, to call plays for him this year. There could be a learning curve for him but Blough might end up being a positive. He is a well respected, up and coming coach. Daniels is a smart quarterback with a very strong arm. He does a great job of going through his progressions and making the right read. Daniels can make plays on the move as both a runner and thrower. He has a knack for making the dramatic play and the moment never seems too big for him. Injuries are a bit of a concern after last year. Plus, he has a smallish frame and runs the ball often.
3.outlook: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is coming off a disappointing sophomore season caused by multiple injuries that limited him to only four full games. The narrative around Daniels has shifted from a young phenom to one of injury worries. Before last season, he had only missed one game due to an injury dating back to his high school career. Daniels will aim to return to his 2024 production, in which he posted one of, if not the, best rookie seasons of all time. The former Heisman winner was fifth in fantasy points per game (21.5) and overall scoring (364.8) that season. That production would have placed Daniels second overall in both categories in 2025 fantasy scoring, only behind Josh Allen. In 2026, Daniels will lead a new offense under David Blough that is quarterback-friendly and highly praised by players. Blough's offense will likely feature a healthy amount of play-action, pre-snap motion, and designed rollouts to get Daniels out in space to maximize his dual-threat ability. The offensive tempo will significantly slow down from a 60-plus percent no-huddle rate the previous two seasons, keeping an improving offensive line fresh to protect Daniels throughout games. The 25-year-old has a rushing cheat code to push for the QB1 title in fantasy football that overshadows his elite arm talent from the pocket. He produced a rookie quarterback record of 891 rushing yards, along with a rookie record 69 percent completion rate and a 100.1 passer rating that ranks fourth all-time for rookie quarterbacks. Managers can draft Daniels with confidence that he will return to his 2024 level of play, with a high floor and immense upside.

4.name: Jalen Hurts
4.comment: Hurts did not have the season most expected, posting some mediocre passing numbers. He averaged just 201.5-passing yards per game. He attempted just 454 passes on the season.  Hurts had one of the best intended air yard averages in football, averaging 9.0 intended air yards per attempt. He did have 20-plus fantasy points 11 of 16 games to finish eighth overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. Hurts was pretty consistent from a fantasy perspective. He has been a top-10 fantasy quarterback five straight seasons. Hurts has 600-plus rushing yards four of five seasons and reached double-digit rushing touchdowns four of those season. The Eagles will have a new offense this year and might be a little more balanced than past years, giving Hurts a few more chances to air it out. Hurts will continue to be the starter in this explosive offense. His arm strength isn't top notch but good enough. His accuracy continues to make strides but he does miss on some throws he should make. He also can hold onto the ball too long at times. The Eagles have a great offensive line and some of the top offensive weapons in football, giving Hurts a great surrounding cast to work with on a weekly basis.
4.outlook: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts rebounded as a passer in 2025, but the rushing output took a hit, leaving him as the standard QB8 for total and per-game points. The entire offense took a step back, though they still relied on the Tush Push by the goal line, which resulted in Hurts scoring eight times on the ground (105 carries, 421 yards). But this followed his eclipsing double-digit rush TD with 139 or more carries in his four previous seasons. This was joined by a 64.8% completion rate for 3,224 yards and a career-best 25 touchdowns and six picks, though he was middle-of-the-pack in most advanced passing metrics. And yet he was the QB3 through eight games, dipping to the QB10 after the Week 9 bye. The question will be how the offense, now under another new coordinator in Sean Mannion, adjusts without A.J. Brown, with additions of Makai Lemon, Eli Stowers, Dontayvion Wicks, and Marquise Brown in tow. The upside and risk is balanced around a RotoBaller site rank and ADP around the 66th pick as the QB7 this summer.

5.name: Joe Burrow
5.comment: Burrow had injury cut short his season, but still had a really productive fantasy season when on the field. He had 20-plus fantasy points five of his eight starts, including three straight to end his season. He had two four-touchdown performances. Burrow had a bad-throw percentage of 11.3 percent, which was the second best in football. He showed great accuracy and decision making throughout the season. Burrow has 4,400-plus yards and 36-plus total touchdowns three of five seasons. Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the game and carries the Bengals offense on a weekly basis. Burrow is the complete package at quarterback. He has a strong arm, moves around the pocket well and can make plays with his legs. He also is very smart and as accurate as any quarterback in the game. He also has good size for the position and is extremely accurate. He rarely makes mistakes.
5.outlook: Burrow is an elite fantasy quarterback capable of finishing first overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He is a top-five option at the position. Look for around 4,500-passing yards, 40 total touchdowns and 200-rushing yards.

6.name: Drake Maye
6.comment: Maye had a huge second season, playing at an MVP level. He led his team to the Super Bowl and was third overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had 12 of 17 games with 20-plus fantasy points. He scored at least a touchdown all but a game. Maye also had a league-best 72 percent completion percentage. Maye had the fifth best on-target percentage in football (79 percent), showing great accuracy. It was quite the breakout season for Maye. The only concern was his finish. He struggled in the playoffs, having a hard time repeating his great play in the regular season. But even with that said, Maye looks to be a star in this league. He is going to be the franchise quarterback for years to come. Maye has a top arm, having the ability to make all the throws needed in the NFL. He is extremely accurate and does well on the deep ball for a young player. He also does well with using his legs and picking up tough yards if needed. He will force some throws, though, as evident by his play in the playoffs.
6.outlook: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye took advantage of an easy schedule and was excellent in his first year under OC Josh McDaniels' offense. Maye was second in MVP voting and threw for 4,394 passing yards and a 31:8 TD:INT ratio while rushing for 450 yards and four scores in 17 games last season. The North Carolina product also completed 72.0% of his passes, sixth-highest in NFL history. Under head Mike Vrabel, Maye led the Pats to a Super Bowl, but New England was crushed by the Seahawks 29-13. The Patriots will look to make another run at the Super Bowl and bolstered their wide receiver depth. New England acquired A.J. Brown from the Eagles and signed free agent WR Romeo Doubs to a four-year, $68 million contract this offseason. With the additions of Brown and Doubs, Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, and Kyle Williams are also returning. Still, the Patriots did move on from Stefon Diggs, who logged 1,013 receiving yards last season. The Patriots will have a much tougher schedule this season, but everything is set for Maye to have another strong fantasy season in 2026. Bills star quarterback Josh Allen has been the fantasy QB1 the past few seasons, but with the addition of Brown and Doubs, can Maye overtake Allen? Not quite yet, as RotoBaller ranks Maye as the fourth-overall QB while projecting him to throw for 4,772 yards and 32 scores in 2026. Once Allen is off the draft board, Maye could be the next QB called by fantasy managers in upcoming drafts, as he is set to build off last year's incredibly efficient campaign.

7.name: Trevor Lawrence
7.comment: Lawrence finally took his game to another level last season. He was fourth overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had seven straight games to end his season with 20-plus fantasy points. He played his best football late, leading the Jaguars to the playoffs. For the season, he had fewer than 20 fantasy points just five times, showing great consistency. Lawrence did a much better job of liming the poor throws, having the 11th best bad-throw percentage in football (14.4 percent). He still struggled with accuracy at times, completing just 60.9 percent of his passes. This remains an area he can improve. Head coach Liam Coen was a huge asset for Lawrence last year and should continue to help Lawrence grow as a quarterback. The Jaguars have some top weapons to work with offensively and could improve on offense even more in their second season under Coen. Lawrence has three of five seasons with 4,000-plus passing yards and 25-plus touchdowns. Lawrence is a very smart quarterback with a plus arm. He isn't a running quarterback but moves around the pocket well and can make plays on the run. He is accurate, especially on shorter throws, but can struggle some with the deep ball accuracy. Lawrence will force throws at times, having double-digit interceptions three seasons.
7.outlook: Heading into the 2026 season as RotoBaller's QB10, Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence may be one of the biggest bargains to be found in the later rounds of fantasy drafts. Lawrence finished 2025 as the QB4 but was even more dominant down the stretch. He was the QB1 over the final ten weeks of the year, and he outpaced the QB2 by more than four points per game after Week 11. Even with Travis Hunter expected to spend more time on the defensive side of the ball in 2026, Lawrence is surrounded by a deep group of pass catchers in Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and tight end Brenton Strange, and the offense as a whole could take another step forward in year two under Liam Coen. Lawrence's fantasy upside was unlocked in part due to his rushing prowess, with the 2021 first overall pick adding 359 yards and nine scores on the ground (both career highs), and with Travis Etienne Jr. and his 56.3 targets per game over the past three seasons heading to New Orleans, Lawrence could see additional scramble opportunities in 2026. Lawrence will need to raise his unimpressive 60.9% completion rate, but with a tangible area of improvement to point to heading into year six, the sky is still the limit if he can finally piece together all elements of his game.

8.name: Justin Herbert
8.comment: Herbert was 10th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had seven games with 20-plus fantasy points. His production did tail off as the season progressed, though, having fewer than 20 points six of his last seven games. The Chargers had injuries along the offensive line and at receiver, though. This really impacted Herbert, who used his legs a lot more to make plays. Herbert ran for a career-high 498 yards. He threw for 3,737 yards and 26 touchdowns to go along with 13 interceptions. He did make a few more mistakes after having less than eight interceptions two straight season. Herbert has at least 20 touchdowns every season in the NFL and 4,300-plus passing yards three of six seasons. Herbert is a really big quarterback with a strong arm. He can make all the throws and withstand the punishment of the NFL. His accuracy is very good and he does a great job of making plays down the field. He also can make play with his legs. Herbert is the complete package at quarterback.
8.outlook: Herbert isn't quite in that elite group but just outside it. He has finished 10th or higher in quarterback scoring four straight seasons. His numbers could improve this year, though, if the Chargers offensive line can hold up and his receivers get better. Consider him a low-end No. 1 for fantasy teams. He can get around 4,000 yards and 30 total touchdowns with few turnovers.

9.name: Caleb Williams
9.comment: Williams had a breakout season, taking his game to a new level. New head coach Ben Johnson was a huge asset for Williams, helping the young quarterback make big strides in year two. Williams was fifth overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had 30 total touchdowns to just seven interceptions. Williams had 10 games with 20-plus fantasy points, showing great consistency. Williams took plenty of chances down the field, averaging 8.5 intended air yards per pass attempt. This was the ninth highest total. It wasn't all good for Williams, though. He had the fourth worst on-target percentage in football (69.8 percent). He also had the fourth worst bad throw percentage (20.7 percent). He did struggle with accuracy, missing on some passes he should make as an NFL starter. Williams made some unbelievable clutch plays throughout the season, showing a knack for coming up big at the crucial moment. He has the makings of a star quarterback for years to come. Williams has a great arm and does well making plays on the move. He is good at improvising and making the big play. Williams has room for improvement, though, especially when it comes to hitting the open receiver. He also doesn't throw a consistent deep ball just yet.
9.outlook: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams followed up a rocky rookie campaign by elevating his play under Ben Johnson, becoming the QB6 last year. The completion rate took a hit, but he made his throws count for more downfield, and the new scheme led to only 24 sacks against after absorbing 68 in '24. Williams' intended air yards per pass attempt bumped up from 7.9 to 8.5 as the next generation of Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, and Colston Loveland got going. "Iceman" led six fourth-quarter comebacks, earning a 77-388-3 rushing line with a receiving TD sprinkled in. Will he turn around in his third season and start using his legs more as a rusher, rather than extending the play for a deep shot? He just showed us that he doesn't need to do that to be a solid top-10 QB, but that would be his path to reaching the top tier. Our RotoBaller rank has him in the top eight next to his ADP around pick 64 as the QB6.

10.name: Dak Prescott
10.comment: Prescott was one of the best fantasy quarterbacks in the game, finishing sixth overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He led the league in completions (404). Prescott threw for 4,552 yards and had 32 total touchdowns to 10 interceptions. Prescott had 20-plus fantasy points 11 of 17 games, showing great consistency. Prescott was one of the most accurate quarterbacks, having a bad throw percentage of just 12.5 percent (sixth best). Prescott has 28 or more touchdowns six of nine seasons. He is an accurate quarterback that normally makes great decisions in a high-volume passing offense. Prescott does a good job of taking care of the football but isn't afraid to take chances down the field. He also can make plays with his legs, having 200-plus rushing yards five seasons.
10.outlook: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott will turn 33 just weeks before the start of his 11th professional season, and with the team making a concerted effort to shore up the defense, the veteran signal-caller may no longer be tasked with putting up 30 points every week to give his team a chance. The Cowboys saw an immediate defensive turnaround after acquiring Quinnen Williams in a mid-season trade, and with a clear focus on one side of the ball through both free agency and the draft, Dallas' pass-heavy game scripts could be shelved in 2026, leading to fantasy dips across the board. That said, at RotoBaller's QB11, Prescott has been severely undervalued for years, and even if his production takes a step back, he still represents clear value in the later rounds of drafts. Across his last four healthy seasons, Prescott has finished as the QB2, QB8, QB3, and QB6, and while playing in at least 16 games, he's finished outside the top 10 only once in his career, all the way back in 2018. With an offensive cast of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson, and Javonte Williams, even if the Cowboys aren't required to approach every game as a track meet, they still have the offensive firepower to finish as one of the highest scoring teams in the NFL, and fresh off a 4,552-yard, 30-touchdown season, Prescott still boasts league-winning potential.

11.name: Jaxson Dart
11.comment: Dart started 12 games his rookie season but still managed to finish 13th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He showed huge fantasy potential, having 10 games with 20-plus fantasy points. He was extremely consistent all season in a starting role. Dart had 24 total touchdowns to just five interceptions. He also ran for almost 500 yards and scored nine rushing touchdowns. The big concern for Dart was the beating he took, suffering multiple concussions. He took some big hits. Dart will need to figure out how to avoid those hits going forward if he hopes to make it through a full season. Dart is going to be the franchise quarterback for the Giants for years to come. He is a playmaker. Dart can make plays with his legs and arm. Dart is a tough quarterback that does well in extending the play and making plays down the field. He is really good on the move whether it comes as a thrower or runner. Dart takes some unnecessary hits, though, and needs to do a much better job of protecting his body as an NFL starter.
11.outlook: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart enters 2026 as one of the more volatile fantasy quarterbacks after flashing real rushing upside as a rookie. Dart played 14 games and started 12 in 2025, completing 216 of 339 passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns, and five interceptions. The passing production was uneven, but his legs changed the fantasy profile. Dart rushed 86 times for 487 yards and nine touchdowns, giving him weekly upside that matters more in Superflex and two-QB formats. He became the starter in Week 4 after Russell Wilson was benched and averaged roughly 22.6 fantasy points per start, though the floor was not always stable. Dart also took 35 sacks, missed two games after a Week 10 concussion, and remains a developing passer entering a new offense under HC John Harbaugh and OC Matt Nagy. Malik Nabers' (knee) recovery from a 2025 knee injury is another key variable, even with Darnell Mooney and Isaiah Likely added to the supporting cast. Dart is currently being drafted as the QB9 on Sleeper, while RotoBaller ranks him 104th overall and QB12. Dart's rushing gives him a path to outperform that range, but he is easier to justify in Superflex than as an aggressive single-QB target.

12.name: Bo Nix
12.comment: Nix had a big second season, finishing seventh overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had 10 of 17 games with 20-plus fantasy points. Nix got plenty of chances to air it out, leading the league in pass attempts (612). He had 30 total touchdowns to 11 interceptions and just finished with less than 4,000-passing yards. Nix had the ninth best on-target percentage in football (77.4 percent). He did a lot of things well in year two and should continue to grow as a player. Nix has 30-plus touchdowns each of his two seasons in the NFL. Nix has a top arm and does well in making plays on the run. He also is a tough quarterback that isn't afraid to lower his shoulder and pick up the extra yard when needed. Nix will force some passes at times, but has gotten better in that area. Nix also is an accurate quarterback for a young player and does very well with the deep ball.
12.outlook: Bo Nix is entering his third season in the NFL, and has performed exceptionally well through his first two seasons both from a fantasy perspective and from a real-football perspective. Nix has finished both of his first two seasons in the league as the QB7, averaging 18.6 and 17.9 fantasy points per game. He offers some rushing stability, never finishing below 356 rushing yards or four scores on the ground in either season. Nix's floor should be elevated with the addition of Jaylen Waddle, giving him a new go-to target. He has yet to eclipse 4,000 yards passing, falling just short last season at 3,931, but should be surrounded by the strongest group of weapons he's seen thus far in 2026. Nix is still recovering from the ankle injury that held him out of the AFC Championship, but he is expected to participate in mandatory minicamp.

13.name: Jared Goff
13.comment: Goff had another solid season but wasn't quite as prolific as he has been in recent years. Goff was ninth overall in fantasy quarterback scoring after finishing sixth the previous season. He has been a top-10 fantasy quarterback four straight seasons, though. He has posted consistent numbers in this high-powered Lions offense. Goff had eight of 17 games with 20-plus fantasy points. He scored 34 touchdowns to just eight interceptions and topped 4,500-passing yards for the third straight season. Goff didn't take many chances down the field once again, averaging just 6.4 air yards per pass attempt. This was good for 37th overall in football. He was very accurate, though, having the sixth best on target percentage in football (78.3 percent). He will continue to start for the Lions and should have plenty of good years left at this stage of his career. The Lions have some of the best young playmakers in football right now and Goff will continue to lead the way for them. The only concern is Goff will be with a new offensive coordinator for the second straight season. He wasn't quite as prolific last season with Ben Johnson gone. Goff is a pocket passer that is accurate and sees the field well. He has a plus arm that can make all the throws. Goff has improved on the deep ball since entering the league and does well in hitting his receivers in stride on shorter throws. He will make some poor decisions when pressured and force throws, but limit his interceptions despite that.
13.outlook: Lions quarterback Jared Goff has finished as the QB10, QB7, QB6, and QB9 across his last four seasons in Detroit, and despite working in an era where quarterbacks of his archetype are starting to play into their late-30s and beyond, the 31-year-old former first overall pick has fallen all the way to QB18 in RotoBaller's redraft rankings. As one of the more durable quarterbacks in the league, Goff has missed only five games over the past nine seasons, and none since 2021, and his well-documented home/road splits have made his boom games comparatively easy to forecast, making him the perfect platoon quarterback for drafters opting for a two-quarterback or streaming approach to the position. In what was considered a down year for the Lions' offense in 2025, Goff threw for 4,564 yards and 34 touchdowns to only eight interceptions. After a one-year adjustment period without offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, the Lions hired Drew Petzing to run the unit, fresh off a 2025 season with the Cardinals in which he led journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett to a QB5 pace across his 12 starts. With nine of 11 offensive starters returning to a team that has not ranked outside the top five in yards per game since 2021, fantasy managers who forego the position in the early rounds of drafts should be looking to take advantage of Goff's mispricing.

14.name: Baker Mayfield
14.comment: Mayfield had a bit of a disappointing season last year. He dealt with a lot of injuries at receiver, though, and the loss of offensive coordinator Liam Coen likely played a factor as well. He still had 26 touchdowns to 11 interceptions but his yardage numbers were down, throwing for 3,693 after two straight 4,000-yard seasons. Mayfield was just 12th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring after being top-10 his previous two seasons. He started his season great, having 20-plus fantasy points six straight games. But he topped 20 fantasy points four of his last 11 games. He struggled some getting on the same page as his receiver, completing just 63 percent of his passes. Mayfield gets another new offensive coordinator this season, Zac Robinson, and hopefully a healthy group of receivers for a full year. The Bucs have a great group of receivers for Mayfield to work with when healthy. Mayfield has topped 4,000-passing yards and 29-plus touchdowns two of three seasons in Tampa. He has excelled since taking over as the starter for the Bucs. Mayfield is a very athletic quarterback that does a great job of making plays on the move. He is a playmaker with a strong arm. He still will force some passes but has really improved his accuracy in recent years.
14.outlook: Even though his pass attempts in 2025 and 2024 were nearly identical, Baker Mayfield lost 36.5% of his passing touchdown production in one season (41 in 2024, 26 in 2025). Add in a decline from three rushing touchdowns to one as well, and fantasy managers were left with a drop of about 100 fantasy points after his 2024 career year. In 2026, Mayfield's favorite weapon, wide receiver Mike Evans, is off to San Francisco, leaving Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, and the backfield tandem of Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. Many of the Buccaneers' offensive weapons were hurt last season, including Mayfield himself. Mayfield, Godwin, Evans, Egbuka, and Jalen McMillan all missed significant time, but that group should be healthy heading into the new season. With a healthy roster and a new offensive coordinator in Zac Robinson, Mayfield has a good shot of returning to the level of a top-10 quarterback, even though he is being drafted much closer to QB20.

15.name: Brock Purdy
15.comment: Injuries were an issue for Purdy last year but he played well when on the field. He played nine games and had six games with 20-plus fantasy points. Purdy had three-touchdown games three of his last four to end his season. He 23 total touchdowns to 10 interceptions. If he plays a full season, Purdy throws for 4,094 yards, scores 43 total touchdowns and has 19 interceptions. His turnovers were a bit of an issue but the rest of his numbers were off the charts. And Purdy had the best on-target percentage in football (82.2 percent), showing great accuracy throughout the season. He completed 69.4 percent of his passes. Purdy has produced at a high level since taking over as the 49ers starter. He is yet to play a full season, though, and has double-digit interceptions three straight years. Purdy is an accurate passer that takes what the opposition gives him. He doesn't force passes and can make plays with his legs if needed. He moves around the pocket well and is a good fit for the 49ers offense. He knows his limitations and is capable of the big play when given the chance.
15.outlook: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy was limited to nine games in 2025 thanks to a shoulder injury and a persistent case of turf toe. He finished the year with 2,167 passing yards, 20 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. Over half of Purdy's season-long fantasy production came in Weeks 15 through 17, when he averaged 298 passing yards per game, threw for 11 touchdowns to two interceptions, and ran in two additional scores. In his other six games, Purdy was held to 200 passing yards or fewer four times and averaged 13.6 fantasy points per game. Question marks surround the state of Purdy's pass-catching corps entering 2026. Jauan Jennings left via free agency, Brandon Aiyuk's discord with the 49ers drags on, and George Kittle's (Achilles) availability for the start of the season in question. Ricky Pearsall is still unproven after injuries sidelined him for half of 2025. Key offseason acquisition Mike Evans also missed nine games due to injury last year, has a history of hamstring issues, and will be 33 at the start of the season. Purdy targeted Christian McCaffrey more than anyone in 2025, and that may be the case again in 2026, which limits Purdy's yardage potential. Purdy is the QB11 in RotoBaller's current rankings, but not much separates him from the other quarterbacks in his tier, which includes Jaxson Dart, Patrick Mahomes (knee), and Matthew Stafford. Fantasy managers who wait to draft a quarterback might want to pass over Purdy for one with a clearer path to success in 2026.

16.name: Matthew Stafford
16.comment: Stafford had maybe the best season of his career at age 37. He had an MVP season, finishing third overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He rebounded in a big way after finishing just 19th the previous year. Stafford had 11 games with 20-plus fantasy points, including five with 30-plus points. Stafford led the league in passing touchdowns and had a career-best 46 for the season. He also led the league in passing yards (4,707). Stafford attempted a ton of passes down the field, having the third highest intended air yards per pass attempt (9.0). Stafford is 37 years old and has a bit of an injury history, so there are some question marks for him even after his huge season. Stafford has been a top-10 fantasy quarterback five of his last 11 seasons. Stafford has 10 4,000-yard seasons and five of those seasons with 30-plus scores. Stafford has a huge arm, moves around the pocket well and is a big, strong quarterback. He will force some passes, though, having 52 interceptions his five seasons with the Rams.
16.outlook: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is coming off of the best statistical season of his career, throwing for a career-high 46 touchdowns while finishing as the QB3 in fantasy. Stafford won the MVP, playing at the highest level of his 17-year career, yet the Rams remained focused on the future of the position in the 2026 NFL Draft when they selected Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson with the thirteenth pick in the first round. The selection of Simpson does not put any immediate pressure on Stafford, but the addition of his eventual replacement does add extra incentive to remain playing at the highest level possible. Los Angeles returns both Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, reuniting Stafford with the lethal receiving duo that allowed him to play at an MVP level. There are no indicators that his play will fall off this season, and he should be among the top quarterbacks off of the board in 2026 fantasy drafts.

17.name: Patrick Mahomes
17.comment: Mahomes was having a great rebound season before tearing his ACL in Week 15. He has a long road back but expectations to be ready for Week 1. We should know more as the season draws near but nothing is certain at this point. Mahomes was still 11th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring despite playing 14 games. He threw for 3,587 yards and 22 touchdowns with 11 interceptions. And Mahomes made a lot more plays with his legs last year, rushing for 422 yards and five touchdowns. Both rushing totals were career highs for Mahomes. You have to wonder how he will view rushing the ball going forward after tearing his ACL last year. Mahomes had nine of 14 games with 20-plus fantasy points, including four games with 30-plus points. He was consistent and prolific many weeks. Mahomes has 4,000-yard seasons all but two in his career. He ha at least 37 touchdown passes four of eight seasons. He remains arguably the best quarterback in the game right now. Mahomes might have more ability than any quarterback. Mahomes has a rocket for an arm. He reads defenses well and can make big-time plays while on the move. He makes throws that make your jaw drop. The Chiefs also have some improving, young weapons in the passing game.
17.outlook: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) suffered a torn ACL/LCL in Week 15 against the Los Angeles Chargers, ending his season. Before the injury, Mahomes was set to bounce back in fantasy from a mediocre 2024 by throwing for 3,587 yards and a 22:11 TD:INT ratio while rushing for a career-high 422 yards and five scores in 14 games. According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Chiefs and Mahomes are both "leaning into this Week 1 possibility" that he'll be ready to go for the first Monday night game of the 2026 season against the Denver Broncos. He continues to progress in OTAs as he's been participating in 7-on-7 drills. The Chiefs added Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker, and wide receivers Rashee Rice (knee), Xavier Worthy, and tight end Travis Kelce are all returning. However, Rice is recovering from arthroscopic knee surgery but is expected to be ready for training camp. Mahomes will see a decline in rushing yards this upcoming season with the injury on top of the addition of Walker. Fantasy managers should monitor his status throughout training camp, but all signs point to Mahomes being ready for Week 1. RotoBaller projects the 30-year-old to accumulate 287 fantasy points and throw for 29 touchdowns, while ranking him QB13 heading into upcoming fantasy football drafts. Mahomes might not be projected to finish as a top-10 fantasy quarterback, but there is no reason to doubt Mahomes as a borderline QB1/high-end QB2 in 2026 given his very successful past.

18.name: Tyler Shough
18.comment: Shough did not open his rookie season as the starter but eventually took over and played really well in that role. He had 20-plus fantasy points six straight games to end his season and seven of his last eight games. Shough was super consistent as the starter for the Saints. He had 13 total touchdowns to six interceptions in 11 games (nine starts). He completed an impressive 67.6 percent of his passes. And his intended air yards per pass attempt was 8.3, so Shough was taking chances down the field. Shough showed a lot as a rookie and should continue to get better with more seasoning. Shough is a big quarterback with a big arm. He also moves around the pocket well for a man of his size. He can force some throws because of his big arm, but did a good job of limiting those throws last season.
18.outlook: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough finished 2025 with 2,384 passing yards, 10 passing touchdowns, three rushing touchdowns, and a 67.6% completion rate across 11 games. He also produced one of his best games late in the season, throwing for 333 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over the Titans. He was so good down the stretch, in fact, that he was QB5 in overall fantasy points from Weeks 12-18. The fantasy appeal for Shough comes from the possibility that he is still undervalued despite his rushing ability, improved offensive weapons, and a head coach who plays at the league's fastest pace. His accuracy, rushing, and weapons give him a strong foundation, and his late-season surge showed that his ceiling may be much higher than we originally thought. If the Saints continue building around him in 2026, with new weapons in rookie Jordyn Tyson and running back Travis Etienne Jr., Shough has the potential to become one of the best quarterback values in fantasy drafts because his cost will likely remain outside the top 100 picks.

19.name: Malik Willis
19.comment: Willis started the Week 17 game and played in relief the previous week, producing very well in those two games. He scored 35.4 fantasy points in Week 17 against the Ravens, scoring three total touchdowns. For the season, he completed 85.7 percent of his passes and had five total touchdowns without an interception. Willis has looked good in two season as the top backup for the Packers. He got a chance to sit and learn, which seemed to be beneficial for him. He gets his chance to start again this year, signing a big deal with the Dolphins to become their No. 1 quarterback. Miami is hoping for a resurgence similar to Baker Mayfield and Sam Darnold, players that started their careers poorly but have turned it around. Willis still remains a bit raw (six career starts in four seasons) but has plenty of talent. Willis has a huge arm and can make a lot of plays with his legs. His accuracy and decision making seem much better than from earlier in his career.
19.outlook: It's an exciting time for Malik Willis. The former Packer completed 78% of his passes for over 900 yards in reserve duty across two seasons, impressing general managers across the league with his progression as a quarterback. That made him the cream of the crop in the free agent quarterback class. The Miami Dolphins rewarded the backup to Jordan Love with a three-year, $67.5-million contract to be the team's starter this upcoming season. With his rushing abilities (174 yards in three starts with the Packers), Willis is the type of quarterback that fantasy managers love. He doesn't necessarily need strong passing numbers to rack up fantasy points, which is good, because his receiver corps may be the weakest in the league. The Dolphins traded Jaylen Waddle to Denver this offseason, and Tyreek Hill is no longer part of the team. That leaves Malik Washington, Tutu Atwell, Jalen Tolbert, and three middle-round rookies atop the depth chart. If Willis and running back De'Von Achane can keep the offense humming, he'll outplay his mid-to-low-end QB2 ranking. Otherwise, the lack of skill position talent could keep the former third-round pick from enjoying a breakout campaign.

20.name: Kyler Murray
20.comment: Murray had a lost season last year, playing just the first five games because of a foot injury. He had 20-plus fantasy points just one of those five games. Murray averaged less than 200-passing yards per game for the first time in his career. He did complete 68.3 percent of his passes and had six touchdowns to three interceptions. It wasn't all bad for Murray. He signed with the Vikings this offseason and should get first shot to start with his new team. Murray has 3,700-plus passing yards four of seven seasons. He has been very good at times throughout his career but struggled some in recent years. Nothing is certain for him going forward. Murray has a great arm, can make all the throws and use his legs as an asset offensively. He is the complete package at quarterback. He will make bad decisions at times and looks rattled when facing pressure.
20.outlook: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is entering his eighth season in the NFL, his first away from Arizona. Murray has finished as a fantasy QB1 in four of his seven seasons, achieving the finish in every season that he has played at least 14 games. However, Murray has only played more than 11 games in one of the past four seasons. He missed 12 games last year with a foot injury, and didn't look particularly great in the games when he was healthy, prompting Arizona to move on. Murray landed in Minnesota, which has been a great spot for quarterbacks to rejuvenate their careers. If he has it in him to follow in the footsteps of Sam Darnold, Murray could be set for a huge season. Surrounded by Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, and T.J. Hockenson with Kevin O'Connell calling plays, Murray is in the best situation of his career. As long as he wins the QB1 job over J.J. McCarthy, as is expected, he could be in for an astronomical bounce-back.

21.name: Jordan Love
21.comment: Love was 15th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring last year. He had five games with 20-plus fantasy points. He was a little up and down throughout the season but showed some improvements in play from the previous year. Love really improved his accuracy after struggling some in that area last year. He had the ninth best on-target percentage (77.4 percent) in football. Love completed 66.3 percent of his passes, which was his best total as a full-time starter. Love has all the tools to be a top NFL starter but hasn't reached that level yet. He is a big quarterback with a very strong arm. He can make all the throws. His accuracy isn't that of a top quarterback and will need to improve if he hopes to reach that next level. Love also can make some plays with his legs but it isn't a strength of his game.
21.outlook: Since a top-five quarterback finish in 2023, Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love has finished as the QB17 (2024) and QB15 (2025) in total points. Because of his recent performance, Love is currently being drafted as the QB15 for 2026. Is it possible Love can return to an elite level after the team lost Romeo Doubs and now face major legal questions marks with Josh Jacobs? The good news is that Christian Watson is healthy and now has a massive contract to be their WR1. Matthew Golden finally started looking like a first-round receiver at the end of last season. And Tucker Kraft appears to be on track to return from a torn ACL in Week 1. With all of his weapons deployed and ready, Love could vault back into the top ten on the back of his career 7.6 yards per attempt. If Love can get anywhere close to his four rushing touchdowns from 2024, this could be a career year for the sixth-year veteran.

22.name: Sam Darnold
22.comment: A move to Seattle was a good one for Darnold, having his second straight good season. He led his new team to the Super Bowl and was 14th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. Darnold was a little up and down for fantasy teams, having four games with fewer than double-digit fantasy points. He also had seven games with 20-plus points. Darnold had some turnover issues, leading the league with 25 turnovers (14 interceptions, 11 fumbles). That was the only negative for Darnold in year one with the Seahawks. He was very accurate, having a career-best 67.7 percent completion percentage. Darnold had the third best on-target percentage (79.8 percent), showing great accuracy. He has been a top-15 fantasy quarterback two straight seasons. He will continue to start in the Seahawks high-powered offense. Seattle can be a little run heavy at times, leading to fewer chances for Darnold. Darnold has a great arm, can make plays down the field, and also moves around the pocket pretty well. He will turn the ball over, though, especially when pressured. Darnold is not afraid to take chances down the field, having a career 8.1 intended air yards per pass attempt.
22.outlook: The Seattle Seahawks took a chance on Sam Darnold after the Minnesota Vikings told him "no thanks" after 36 total touchdowns in 2024. That decision was one of the biggest reasons Seattle hoisted the Lombardi Trophy in February, as Sam Darnold played an entire postseason without a turnover and led his team to a massive win over the New England Patriots for the title. However, in the regular season, Darnold had 20 total turnovers and threw 10 fewer touchdowns than his excellent 2024 season. He will look to clean that up as the offense is likely to skew more pass-friendly with the departure of Kenneth Walker III and the emergence of Jaxson Smith-Njigba. Last season, Darnold threw for the highest yards per attempt of his career (8.5 yards), so what he might sacrifice in yards will likely be gained back with better efficiency and fewer touchdowns. Darnold is currently being drafted as the QB22 overall, but there is a strong case to be made that Darnold could creep into the top-12 before 2026 is over.

23.name: C.J. Stroud
23.comment: Stroud had his second straight ho-hum season. He did miss some games because of injury but threw for less than 200 yards four of 14 games. He had just four games with 20-plus fantasy points. Stroud was 21st overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had 20 total touchdowns to eight interceptions. He just hasn't progressed much at all since an impressive rookie season. The one positive for Stroud last year was completing a career-best 64.5 percent of his passes. His accuracy was a little better. He will continue to start with the Texans and has a solid group of young receivers to work with on a weekly basis. Hopefully, they can all stay healthy for him this year. Stroud has a great arm and is a fairly accurate passer. He makes big plays at crucial times. Stroud does well in extending the play and making plays on the run. He has good athletic ability, but is not much of a running quarterback. Stroud normally makes good decisions with the football. He does make some bad throws, though, and has forced some throws in recent years.
23.outlook: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has a solid arsenal of pass-catching weapons to throw the ball to. That didn't seem to change a lot last year -- he still struggled to perform well. Wide receiver Nico Collins continues to play at an elite level, and second-year WRs Jaylin Noel and Jayden Higgins will likely be improved after they got off to slow starts in their rookie seasons. WR Tank Dell (knee) should return at some point, but may never be his old self. Stroud has struggled to play consistently, even in his rookie year, where he relied on explosive plays to pump his passing numbers. The starter has struggled behind a poor offensive line. To his credit, that should improve, but the underlying metrics aren't pretty. And Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley bafflingly didn't make heavy use of pre-snap and mid-snap motion, which hurts the offense. The optimistic scenario for Stroud feels like that of a high-end QB2, which makes him not a priority for non-superflex fantasy leagues.

24.name: Bryce Young
24.comment: Young didn't exactly have a breakout season but enjoyed his best to date. He was 19th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had just five games with 20-plus fantasy points but three of those games came after Week 10 He had a bit of an awakening down the stretch. Young had 25 total touchdowns to 11 interceptions. Young made big strides with his accuracy. He had the eighth worst on-target percentage in 2024 but had the eighth-best last season (77.9 percent). This is quite the turnaround. He will look for even more improvement in year four. This might be a make or break season for the young quarterback. Young has all the tools to be a solid NFL quarterback. He is a pretty accurate quarterback with a solid arm. He moves around the pocket well and can make plays on the run. His lack of size is a concern but hasn't held him back to date. Young has held up pretty well.
24.outlook: Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young had his best season yet, throwing for the most yards and touchdowns while going 8-8 after a combined 6-22 record in his first two years. The problem for us, and Carolina, is that the bar was set quite low, so new highs meant only 3,011 yards and 23 TDs en route to a QB19 finish. Also, 2024's willingness to scramble in the red zone that led to six rush TDs gave way to a more modest 54-216-2 line in '25. He has the athleticism to punish defenses who don't keep him contained, but Dave Canales is not designing around it. If anything, Canales looks to have engineered things around Young's limits. The two games we saw him pushed beyond 35 pass attempts led to 776 yards and six TDs (at ARI, at ATL), but eight games yielded 25 or fewer attempts. Even last year, Young's 6.4 intended air yards per attempt was near the bottom of the leaderboard. Perhaps this will change with Year 2 Tetairoa McMillan and a full, healthy season from Jalen Coker. Third-rounder Chris Brazzell II could also push the disappointing Xavier Legette out of the rotation. But the majority of what we've seen has fantasy managers tepidly picking him as the QB26 near pick 160 by late June, which mirrors his RotoBaller ranking. He's only a 2QB/Superflex option for now.

25.name: Cam Ward
25.comment: Ward was 22nd overall in fantasy quarterback scoring his rookie season. He was up and down as expected, but played his best football late in the season, which is encouraging. He had multiple touchdowns four of his last five games and had 20-plus fantasy points two of his last three. The big issue for Ward last year was a lack of accuracy, completing just 59.8 percent of his passes. Ward had an on-target percentage of just 72.6 percent, which was the ninth worst total in football. He also took the most sacks in all of football (55). This led to plenty of struggles throwing the ball on a weekly basis. The Titans lacked top options for Ward to work with offensively, though, so a solid offseason should be a positive for him. Plus, Ward gets to work with a new coaching staff this season. Brian Daboll takes over as the offensive coordinator for the Titans and should be a huge plus for Ward's development. Ward has a great arm and can make all the throws. He does great on the move and making plays outside the pocket. He will force some throws, though, and doesn't always get his passes out on time. He isn't much of a running quarterback but can makes some plays with his legs if needed.
25.outlook: Cam Ward's rookie season, when seen as a whole, was an abject disaster. The number one overall pick had a league-low 5.9 yards per attempt, threw fewer than one touchdown per game, and had 14 turnovers, including seven lost fumbles. He had one of the worst supporting casts in the league and was running a system that often looked like it was stuck in the mud. However, Cam Ward scored at least 15 fantasy points in all weeks of the fantasy playoffs, something only seven quarterbacks were able to do. In 2026, the Tennessee Titans overhauled their coaching staff with Robert Salah as head coach and Brian Daboll as the offensive coordinator. They also drafted Carnell Tate fourth overall and signed Wan'Dale Robinson, a favorite of Diboll. Calvin Ridley is returning from a broken leg, and rookie Elic Alymanor showed flashes last year. With all these weapons, this will be the season where fantasy managers start to see if Cam Ward has top-12 quarterback potential. For now, his ADP as QB24 is probably the safest bet, but there is absolutely room for him to grow and outpace that rank.

26.name: Jacoby Brissett
26.comment: Brissett had the best season of his career, getting a chance to serve as the starter for the Cardinals much of the year. He didn't take over as the starer until Week 6 but was still 16th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. Brissett had 20-plus fantasy points 10 of 12 starts. If he plays a full season, Brissett throws for 4,087 yards and 33 touchdowns with 11 interceptions. That would equate to 387.2 fantasy points, good for fifth best in football. He had quite the season and could be the starter for the Cardinals open the year. Brissett is a top athlete that can make all the throws. He moves around the pocket well and can make plenty of plays with his feet when needed. He struggles with accuracy down the field at times but did better in that area last season.
26.outlook: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett came out of nowhere to gunsling his way into fantasy glory, standing as the QB7 between Weeks 6-17 despite a 1-11 record on the gridiron. The opportunity to play arose after Kyler Murray suffered a mid-foot sprain in Week 5 that ultimately shut him down for the season. Thrust into the spotlight, Brissett's 12 total starts led to 3,366 yards and a 23:8 TD:INT ratio, adding 37 rushes for 166 yards and one TD in that timeframe. While the volume cooled a bit during the fantasy playoffs, Brissett would attempt at least 40 passes in six consecutive games to force his way atop fantasy ranks by pure volume. He showed rapport with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson as Marvin Harrison Jr. and the entire running back corps dealt with injuries. We must mention that Brissett's renaissance has led to a contract dispute, as he wants more security than the $1.5 million in guaranteed money he's due in 2026. For now, he's "holding in," and didn't practice at the mandatory minicamp, as negotiations proceed. That will need to be sorted out, or else Arizona will pivot to Gardner Minshew II or Carson Beck, as unlikely as that seems. The fears that last season was a perfect storm against Brissett's middling track record, along with the contract uncertainty, has resulted in an early QB30 ADP (197). We are a bit more bullish at QB27, happily targeting the ceiling seen roughly 20 picks ahead of that.

27.name: Aaron Rodgers
27.comment: Rodgers had a solid first season in Pittsburgh, leading his new team to the playoffs. He was just 18th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring, though. Rodgers had just four games all season with 20-plus fantasy points. He did not have one 300-yard passing games. Rodgers averaged just 6.0 intended air yards per pass attempt, which was the fourth lowest in football. He took few chances down the field in the Steelers offense. The positives were Rodgers limited turnovers once again (seven interceptions) and led his team to the playoffs. Rodgers has not been much of a fantasy option in recent seasons, finishing outside the top 10 four straight seasons. He has been an elite player throughout his career. Rodgers has more than 30 total touchdowns 10 of 18 seasons. Rodgers also has at least two rushing touchdowns 10 of the last 18 seasons. His rushing totals have gone down as he has gotten older, though, and should continue to dwindle. He still has a plus arm and is an accurate passer.
27.outlook: Future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers opted out of retirement and signed a one-year contract to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The 42-year-old threw for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns, and seven interceptions while rushing for 61 yards and a score in 16 games for the Steelers last season. Rodgers also averaged a measly 6.1-yard average target per depth. He showed signs of his age as the season went on, surpassing 250 yards just three times while throwing for just eight touchdowns over his last 10 games. The Steelers hired Mike McCarthy as the team's head coach this offseason. Rodgers and McCarthy spent 13 years together with the Green Bay Packers from 2006-2018. Pittsburgh added some weapons for Rodgers by acquiring wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. from the Colts and drafting Alabama wideout Germie Bernard in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. DK Metcalf, Jaylen Warren, Pat Freiermuth, and Darnell Washington are also returning, giving Rodgers a solid supporting cast for his final season in the NFL. Rodgers is ranked QB29 in the latest RotoBaller rankings, and with limited upside, he is mainly a QB3 in Superflex leagues or a bye-week replacement in a plus matchup.

28.name: Fernando Mendoza
28.comment: Mendoza was there first overall pick in this year's draft. He is going to be the Raiders starter for years to come. He will compete with veteran Kirk Cousins to start from day one this year. Mendoza is a highly accurate quarterback with a solid arm. He does a great job of being on time with his throws. He can make all the throws and is good in pressure situations. Mendoza isn't the best on the move, though, and is not the most mobile quarterback.
28.outlook: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza enjoyed a stellar final collegiate season at Indiana, tallying 3,535 passing yards, 48 total touchdowns, and just six interceptions en route to a Heisman Trophy Award, undefeated season, and College Football National Championship. He was the clear-cut No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are question marks in Year 1 as a pro. For one, Mendoza is a tactical scrambler, but he's unlikely to make a big impact on the ground at the next level. Without offering much rushing upside, he'll need to be a prolific and efficient passer to be a starter in Single-QB formats, which would be a surprise in 2026 with a wide receiver room consisting of Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, and Dont'e Thornton Jr. Tight end Brock Bowers is fantastic, but there isn't much to be excited about among pass-catchers otherwise in Las Vegas. Combine the worst wide receiver room in the NFL with a typical rookie learning curve, and it's tough to imagine consistent fantasy success for Mendoza right away. He could also sit out a significant amount of his rookie season behind Kirk Cousins. All in all, he's a fine but not ideal QB2 option in Superflex leagues, but he's best left for the waiver wire in most 1QB setups. In dynasty setups, his value is much stronger, and hopefully, the Raiders will surround him with talent in the years to come.

29.name: Geno Smith
29.comment: Smith started most of the season for the Raiders, his first with the team. He was erratic in an offense that struggled much of the season. Smith finished 24th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had three games with 20-plus fantasy points. Smith completed a high percentage of passes (67.4 percent) but led the league with 17 interceptions. He made a lot of mistakes and struggled to move the offense. He has struggled each of his last two seasons but could get another shot to start this year with the Jets. Smith is an extremely accurate quarterback but will turn the ball over. He can make plays with his legs and does well in extending the play to make plays down the field.
29.outlook: The New York Jets acquired quarterback Geno Smith from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick and a 2026 seventh-round pick. Smith will return to the team that drafted him in the second round of the 2013 NFL Draft. The 35-year-old signed a two-year, $75 million contract an offseason ago to be the Raiders' starting QB. The veteran struggled behind a shaky o-line and threw a league-high 17 interceptions last year. Las Vegas cleaned house during the offseason by firing head coach Pete Carroll and dealing Smith to the Jets. The Jets didn't bring in any real competition for Smith at quarterback; the job is his for at least this year. New York is banking on the veteran to return to his glory days in Seattle. Smith will have star wide receiver Garrett Wilson catching passes, and drafted tight end Kenyon Sadiq (16th) and wide receiver Omar Cooper (30th) in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Running back Breece Hall is also returning after signing a three-year, $45 million extension with the Jets this offseason. The o-line is solid, but outside of Hall, Wilson, Sadiq, and Cooper, the Jets lack offensive weapons. Smith did run into some trouble this offseason. According to Rich Cimini of ESPN, Smith is being investigated in relation to an incident in June in which a woman accused him of battery. No charges have been filed yet, and the case is pending investigation. If Smith is not disciplined or suspended, he is QB31 in the latest RotoBaller rankings and is mainly an option in superflex leagues.

30.name: Michael Penix Jr.
30.comment: Penix had an uneven first season as the full-time starter in Atlanta. He suffered a torn ACL in Week 11, getting knocked from the rest of the season. Penix had just three of 10 games with 20-plus fantasy points before the injury. He completed 60.1 percent of his passes and had a bad throw percentage of 24 percent, which was the second worst in football. Needless to say, Penix had some accuracy issues. Penix now has Tua Tagovailoa to compete with for the starting job in Atlanta. Penix would seem to be the better option of the two, but nothing is guaranteed. And with him returning from a major injury. Penix might not be ready for the start of the season. Penix has a great arm and throws a great deep ball because of that. He can get the ball out of his hand in a hurry. He will struggle some when forced from the pocket and miss on some throws he should make. Penix doesn't throw great on the run. And he has endured plenty of accuracy issues to start his career.
30.outlook: Penix is a bit of a question mark this year. He might not be ready for Week 1 and has Tagovailoa looking to unseat him as the starter. We expect Penix to start when healthy, but he'll need to perform to keep the job. He is worth a late-round look for fantasy teams. Expect some big games but he might disappear in others. He could be a good platoon player if he make some strides in year three.

31.name: Daniel Jones
31.comment: Jones was having his best season as a pro before tearing his Achilles' in Week 14. It was a terrible time for Jones to get hurt. He still finished 18th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring despite missing the last four games of the season. Jones has seven games with 20-plus fantasy points. If he plays a full year, Jones throws for 4,054 yards and scores 34 total touchdowns. He completed a career-best 68 percent of his passes. Jones had the seventh best on-target percentage in football (78 percent), showing great accuracy throughout the season. Jones has a long road back from his serious injury but when healthy, he should assume the Colts starting quarterback job once again. He earned it with his play last year. Jones is a tall quarterback with a strong arm and quick release. He can be a very accurate passer, especially on shorter throws. Jones tries to force some throws, but isn't afraid to take chances down the field. He also uses his legs well, rushing for more than 700 yards in 2022. Jones will make some mistakes and injuries have been an issue throughout his career.
31.outlook: Daniel Jones was on pace for a career resurgence his first year in Indianapolis before a torn Achilles in Week 14 ended his season prematurely. Before the injury, Jones was QB13 in fantasy points per game, thanks to his 19 passing touchdowns and five rushing touchdowns. With Jones not even gauranteed to be back by Week 1, and the team surely not going to test his injured Achilles with sneaks around the goal line, his spot as the QB27 in 2026 drafts makes sense. It may be Week 5 before Jones steps onto a field. In addition, the Colts lost Michael Pittman and made no attempt to replace him. That leaves new WR1 Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren, and Josh Downs as the receiving weapons for Jones. In the early part of the season, there should be plenty of Jonathan Taylor, and there is no reason for the Colts to abandon that plan, even when Jones returns. He is a bench/IR stash at best this summer.

32.name: Shedeur Sanders
32.comment: Sanders was buried on the depth chart early his rookie season but eventually got his chance and kept the starting job after getting his chance. He started the last seven games of the season. Sanders completed just 56.6 percent of his passes and had eight total touchdowns to 10 interceptions. He had more than 15 fantasy points just one of his games. The big issue for Sanders was a lack of accuracy. Sanders had an on-target percentage of just 69.6 percent, which was the third worst in all of football. He was pressured more than any other quarterback, getting pressured 40.3 percent of his drop backs. All the pressure likely led to a lot of his poor throws. Sanders will compete for the straiten job this year with a host of options in Cleveland. And a new coaching staff should be a positive for the entire offense, including Sanders. Sanders is a fairly accurate quarterback that is physically gifted. He can make all the throws and does well at extending the play to make a big play. He does tend to hold onto the ball too long and can take some big hits because of that.
32.outlook: After a polarizing slide during the 2025 NFL Draft, Shedeur Sanders' rookie campaign came with virtually no guarantee to see the field as the second quarterback drafted by the Cleveland Browns last year. Much to the chagrin of his fervent fanbase, Sanders was given few preseason opportunities in Cleveland's four-quarterback race, and only after trades of veterans Kenny Pickett and Joe Flacco did Sanders' path to playing time arrive. It was via a Week 11 injury to then-starter Dillon Gabriel, who struggled to a (1-5) record and had issues pushing the ball vertically, per a 6.4 average depth of target (aDOT). Sanders' increased size and arm strength made an immediate impact. He was named the starter in Week 12 and never gave the job back, posting a (3-4) record on the strength of the team's defense. The counting stats for the former Colorado star were disappointing, including just 6.6 yards per pass attempt and a 7:10 TD:INT ratio. The Browns offense completely bottomed out due to offensive line injuries, a lack of perimeter weapons, and a Week 16 season-ending ankle injury to Quinshon Judkins. Deshaun Watson (Achilles) missed the entire 2025 season due to an Achilles injury. Watson will have $45 million guaranteed his way this year. The embattled former Pro Bowler has the inside track to beat out Sanders for the starting job. If Watson struggles, the team would presumably take a second look at Sanders before committing to a quarterback in what projects to be a stellar 2027 draft class for passers. The Browns' QB1 won't be a priority in standard fantasy formats, but committing to a duo of Watson and Sanders in superflex leagues could be an intriguing solution to a roster's QB2 spot following upgrades on the offensive line and at wide receiver in April's draft. The Browns drafted wide recievers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, and OT Spencer Fano with their first three picks in the 2026 NFL Draft. New head coach Todd Monken will also call plays this season. Projected to start 2026 on the bench, Sanders, specifically, slots 299th overall in RotoBaller's PPR rankings, but if he's ever presented the opportunity to start, he was quietly 14th in rushing yards per game among quarterbacks (21.1) if some of these systemic improvements aid his passing efficiency.

33.name: Tua Tagovailoa
33.comment: Tagovailoa was 25th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. He had some big games but struggled with turnovers and was eventually benched late in the season for rookie Quinn Ewers. Tagovailoa had a career-high 15 interceptions in 14 games. And Tagovailoa continues to take few chances down the field, averaging just 6.7 interned air yards per pass attempt. This was the eighth worst average in football. His career is at a bit of a crossroads. He heads to Atlanta this year and likely opens the season as their starter with Michael Penix returning from major injury. If he plays well, Tagovailoa could keep the starting job all season. Tagovailoa can make all the throws and does well on the move. He has some struggles with accuracy down the field, though, and will force some throws. He is best on short, quick throws, getting the ball out in a hurry. He also doesn't have great size for the position, which has caused some injury issues. He might be another concussion away from retiring. And he will struggle some with his accuracy on deep throws.
33.outlook: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa has seen his fantasy value drop year after year since throwing for 4,620 yards and 29 touchdowns on his way to a QB9 finish in 2023. After two down years and his eventual release from the Dolphins, Tagovailoa heads into his first season with the Falcons as RotoBaller's QB31. 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. tore his ACL in Week 11 of the 2025 season, potentially giving Tagovailoa the inside track to starter's reps to begin the year. However, with Penix already into his third professional season, this marks the last chance the team has to evaluate him before deciding whether to pick up his fifth-year option ahead of the 2027 season, meaning they'll likely want him back on the field as soon as he's ready. Outside of deep superflex leagues, Tagovailoa is unlikely to be drafted in 2026, but should Penix's recovery timeline put him on track to miss time early or even begin the year on the Physically Unable to Perform List, the Falcons' opening slate of the schedule is at least worth monitoring. With an improved supporting cast of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts, a healthy, starting Tagovailoa is still capable of providing relevance as a streamer in plus-matchups.

34.name: Deshaun Watson
34.comment: Watson missed all of last year, recovering from a torn Achilles' suffered the previous season. Watson has been a disaster since taking over as the starting quarterback in Cleveland. He has yet to play a full season and has 19-touchdown passes to 12 interceptions while completing just 61.2 percent of his passes. He might get a chance to compete for the starter's job this year but nothing is certain with Watson after the last few seasons. Before his last four seasons with the Browns, Watson had 30-plus touchdowns three straight seasons and 4,000-yard seasons two of three. He has not been the same player since signing a big contract with the Browns. Watson is a great athlete and top playmaker. Watson is a dual threat that can make big plays with his arm and legs. Watson has 400-plus rushing yards three seasons. He will force some throws at times, which has been an issue in recent seasons, and his accuracy is a concern at this point of his career. Plus, he just doesn't seem to see the field very well, making the wrong read at times.
34.outlook: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (Achilles) missed all of last season with an Achilles injury. He initially tore his Achilles in 2024 and re-aggravated the injury in January of last year. Watson is finally back and will need to beat out second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders for the starting job. Watson has been unable to stay on the field, having played only 19 games from 2022-2024. The 30-year-old struggled when he did play, averaging 6.0 YPA and throwing for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, while rushing for 465 yards on 93 attempts and three scores in those 19 contests. The Browns brought in former Baltimore OC Todd Monken as the new head coach this offseason, who has yet to name a starter, as Watson and Sanders will battle it out during training camp. Cleveland did add some weapons by drafting wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in the first and second rounds of the 2026 NFL Draft. Running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. are returning, and veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is also coming back. Even if Watson wins the QB job over Sanders, he is coming off a major injury, hasn't played since 2024, and the chances of him turning back the clock to his glory days in Houston are very slim. Watson is ranked QB32 in the latest RotoBaller rankings and is mainly an option in Superflex leagues only heading into upcoming fantasy football drafts.

35.name: Kirk Cousins
35.comment: Cousins started about half the season for the Falcons, finding his way into the lineup because of an injury to starter Michael Penix. Cousins probably played a little better than he did his first season in Atlanta, but not much. He had 11 total touchdowns to five interceptions and two games with 20-plus fantasy points. Cousins completed just 61.7 percent of his passes and had a 16.1 percent bad throw percentage, which was the second worst total of his career. He had a tendency to miss on some throws he should probably make. Cousins heads to the Raiders this year to help mentor Francisco Mendoza as he transitions to franchise quarterback for the team. Cousins might start early in the year if the Raiders don't feel Mendoza is ready. Cousins isn't a flashy quarterback but a productive pocket passer. He doesn't have a huge arm but is fairly accurate. Turnovers are an issue, though, having 13-plus interceptions three of six seasons.
35.outlook: Kirk Cousins was released by the Atlanta Falcons earlier in the offseason and later signed a two-year, $12.5 million contract with the Las Vegas Raiders. Cousins filled in as the Falcons' starting quarterback midseason once Michael Penix Jr. (knee) suffered a season-ending injury. The 37-year-old appeared to have lost a step, throwing for 1,721 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions, and adding a rushing score through 10 games for Atlanta last season. He threw for over 200 yards just twice, and his 6.4 YPA was ranked 29th in the league. Now with the Raiders, Cousins is reunited with new head coach Klint Kubiak, who worked with the Vikings as an OC and QBs coach during some of the veteran's best years. However, the Raiders selected Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, setting the stage for Cousins to serve as the bridge quarterback until Mendoza is ready to take over. Star running back Aston Jeanty and All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers return while the Raiders signed former Vikings wide receiver Jalen Nailor to a three-year contract this offseason. Cousins/Mendoza will have Jeanty, Bowers, Nailor, Tre Tucker, Michael Mayer, and Jack Bech as their main targets, but the o-line is shaky at best outside center Tyler Linderbaum. Cousins is ranked QB33 in the latest RotoBaller rankings and, at best, is an option in redraft superflex leagues to pair with Mendoza.

36.name: Riley Leonard
36.comment: Leonard got the start his last game of his rookie season against the best defense in football, Houston. He played well, going 21-of-34 for 270 yard and three total touchdowns with an interception. Leonard looked the part of an NFL starter and should have the inside track to be the top backup for the Colts this year. He could even get some starts with Daniel Jones expected to be sidelined some early in the year as he recovers from his torn Achilles. Leonard is a playmaker. He can do well on designed runs and making plays on the run as a passer. He makes pretty good reads as a passer and has adequate arm strength. Leonard shows good touch and toughness in the pocket.
36.outlook: Leonard could have some value early in the season with Daniel Jones out. But even with that said, he is likely going to be really hit or miss as a starting quarterback. Proceed with caution.

37.name: J.J. McCarthy
37.comment: McCarthy got his first taste of NFL action last year but had a season to forget. He really looked overwhelmed at times. He had 15 total touchdowns to 12 interceptions and completed just 57.6 percent of his passes in 10 starts. He averaged just 163.2-passing yards per game for the season. McCarthy showed his fantasy potential, though, having four games with 20-plus fantasy points.
