He should get first shot to start again this year but will need to make big strides this season if he hopes to keep that job. McCarthy will be on a short leash. McCarthy does well in hitting his receivers in stride and making the tough throw. His arm is just alright, though, and he doesn't throw a great deep ball. He struggled with making the right read last year and missed on a lot of wide open throws. McCarthy will compete and make plays with his legs despite not being the fleetest of foot.
37.outlook: McCarthy has some real potential in this offense but is an obvious wild card after last year. He needs to really up his game this coming season. He is worth a shot for fantasy teams if he keeps the starting job. Just make sure you already have a dependable fantasy starter on your roster. McCarthy can get around 3,000 yards, 25 total touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

38.name: Justin Fields
38.comment: Fields opened the season as the starter for the Jets but was unable to keep the job. He struggled, averaging just 139.9-passing yards per game. He started nine games and had 11 total touchdowns to just one interception. He did limit the turnovers, which was a positive. Fields completed just 62.7 percent of his passes, though, and had a hard time generating points in this offense. From a fantasy perspective, Fields performed well, mainly because of his rushing totals. Fields had five of nine starts with 20-plus fantasy points. He got it done on a weekly basis. Fields signed with the Chiefs to become the top backup to Patrick Mahomes but could be called on to possibly start early in the season with Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL. Fields is young enough to get it going again. Fields has a ton of talent and the makeup of a solid NFL quarterback. He has a terrific arm and can be accurate. Fields is a very good athlete that can make plays with his legs all over the field. He can be turnover prone and accuracy has been an issue for Fields.
38.outlook: Fields is a much better fantasy quarterback than NFL quarterback. His rushing upside gives him a huge weekly ceiling when starting. He is worth a look early in the year if he has to fill in for Mahomes. The potential for some big fantasy games is very possible in this offense.

39.name: Ty Simpson
39.comment: The Rams picked Simpson in the first round of this year's draft, hoping to have found their eventual replacement for Matthew Stafford. Simpson should sit and learn under Stafford. Simpson doesn't have a ton of college starting experience, which is a concern, but showed potential with his chances. He has very good mechanics and makes good decisions with the football. He isn't always on time, though, sometimes holds onto the ball too long. He can move around the pocket pretty well and make some plays on the move.
39.outlook: Unless everything goes sideways for the Los Angeles Rams and the reigning NFL MVP, Matthew Stafford, rookie quarterback Ty Simpson is likely to be a non-factor for fantasy managers this season. Make no mistake, the Rams selected Simpson as a developmental asset they could insert into their lineup in two to three years, as Stafford shows no signs of slowing down. Last season, Stafford led the NFL in passing yards (4,707) and passing touchdowns (46), with Jared Goff the next-closest quarterback in passing touchdowns, a full dozen behind the MVP. If something were to happen to Stafford, Simpson would be in one of the best situations a rookie quarterback could be put into, with Sean McVay calling plays and Davante Adams and Puka Nacua out there catching passes. If Simpson is called into action, expect the offense to feature more intermediate routes. Simpson has a history of holding the ball too long and is known for his mobility, which makes it harder to take downfield shots. Stafford signed a one-year, $55 million contract extension this offseason and will be under contract with the Rams until 2027, making Simpson a high-end pick in dynasty formats. Still, he is mainly a handcuff to Stafford in 2QB/Superflex redraft leagues.

40.name: Carson Beck
40.comment: The Cardinals picked Beck in the third round of this year's draft. He is likely to be the top backup this year but the hope for the Cardinals is he eventually becomes the starter for the team down the road. Beck was a highly successful collegiate quarterback that played in some pro-style offensive schemes. This should help his transition to the pro game. Beck has a solid arm and can make all the throws. He does well when given time to throw but can struggle when under pressure.
40.outlook: With Jacoby Brissett's status still unknown as he looks for some additional compensation after coming in Week 6 and throwing for 3,366 yards. Only Jared Goff had more passing yards over that period than Brissett, who also averaged 19.6 fantasy points per game, the sixth-most among quarterbacks to play in at least 10 games over that period. Arizona signed Garber Minshew this offseason to a $5.39 million deal, while Brissett is set to earn just $4.88 million. Now, as far as Carson Beck is concerned, with Brissett's absence from camp, he's been vibing with his receivers and getting additional reps he likely would not have been getting if Brissett were around. This season may be too soon for Beck to make any fantasy impact, as it is more than likely that Brissett and the Cardinals strike a deal before the start of the season. If not, Minshew has proven that he can be a viable bridge quarterback until Beck is ready to take over in 2027. While Beck's outlook in redraft leagues is not great, he should be rostered in all dynasty formats.

41.name: Marcus Mariota
41.comment: Mariota started eight games and played 11 for the Commanders last year, getting a chance to play often because of injuries to Jayden Daniels. Mariota showed pretty well, having three games with 20-plus fantasy points. He had 11 total touchdowns to seven interceptions. Mariota made a case to be a full-time starter once again in the NFL but re-signed with the Commanders to continue to be their top backup. Mariota has not progressed as expected since entering the NFL in 2015, but shown some flashes of good things. Mariota has good size, a great arm and can make plays on the move. He can make all the throws and also runs well at the position. Turnovers are an issue, though, and his accuracy can be erratic.
41.outlook: Mariota always has potential when starting because he can get some yards on the ground in addition to having some success throwing the ball. But even with the said, he is a bit of a wild card and likely to post erratic numbers based off past history.

42.name: Dillon Gabriel
42.comment: Gabriel got six starts his rookie season and played in 10 games. He had some struggles, though, completing just 59.5 percent of his passes while going 1-5 as the starter for the Browns. He topped 200-passing yards just one of his games. Gabriel did smite turnovers, having just two interceptions compared to seven touchdown passes. His biggest struggle was accuracy, having just a 70.7 percent on-target percentage. Gabriel gets a new coaching staff this year, so it is anyone's guess who they will value as the top signal caller out of this crowded group of quarterbacks. Gabriel should be in the mix to start. Gabriel is a small quarterback but does well in making the right read and getting the ball out on time. He lacks some arm strength, though, and won't make a ton of plays with his legs.
42.outlook: Gabriel could get some chances but nothing is certain right now with so many quarterbacks looking to earn a role. But even if he starts, Gabriel showed last year he would be a stretch for fantasy teams to use.

43.name: Quinn Ewers
43.comment: Ewers started the last three games of his rookie season and played alright. He had three touchdowns to three interceptions and completed 66.3 percent of his passes. Ewers wasn't a huge help to fantasy teams, though, failing to top 20 fantasy points in any of his starts. He will likely be the top backup for the Dolphins this year. Ewers has a strong arm and a quick release. He gets the ball out in a hurry and throws with good accuracy. Ewers doesn't move around the pocket too well, though, and can struggle when pressured, making poor decisions.
43.outlook: Ewers might be worth a look if he gets a few starts. He has some potential for the big game in this offense.

44.name: Joe Flacco
44.comment: Flacco was the starter for two different teams last year. He opened the season with the Browns and was their starter to begin the season. He got traded to the Bengals and took over as their starter in Week 6 because of an injury to Joe Burrow. Flacco topped 20 fantasy points each of his first four starts with the Bengals. He started 10 games total and was 27th overall in fantasy quarterback scoring. Flacco has done well as a top backup and spot starter in recent seasons and should continue to play that role. Flacco has a strong arm and the ability to move around the pocket well. He lacks some accuracy at times and will make some poor decisions when rushed. Flacco has always been a big-time performer in the playoffs, showing well in the big games.
44.outlook: Flacco is always worth a look when getting a chance to play. He is capable of the big game any given week.

45.name: Mac Jones
45.comment: Jones started about half the season for the 49ers last year because of injury and played maybe the best football of his career. He had 13 touchdowns to six interceptions and completed a career-best 69.6 percent of his passes. Jones showed great accuracy, having a 79.1 percent on-target percentage. A new offense and coaching staff to learn from was a huge plus for Jones. He had four games with 20-plus fantasy points. Jones might have earned himself another chance to start in the NFL with his play last season. He remains in San Francisco, though, and will be the top backup to Brock Purdy as long as he is there. Jones has 67 touchdown passes to 50 interceptions for his career. Jones is an accurate quarterback that gets rid of the ball quickly. He lacks a little athleticism, though, but can make some plays out of the pocket. He isn't a statue by any means. He will force some passes and can make poor decisions when pressured.
45.outlook: Jones proved last season he can help fantasy teams in a starting role in this offense. So if forced to start again, Jones is worth grabbing for fantasy teams.

46.name: Taylen Green
46.comment: Cleveland added another quarterback to the mix this offseason, taking Green in the sixth round of this year's draft. He is a big-time talent. Green has the arm to make all the throws and can make plays with his legs. He has great size for the position and might be the best athlete of all the quarterbacks picked in this year's draft. Green has a long throwing motion, though, and will force some throws. He also will hold onto the ball too long, taking more sacks than he should. Green is likely third on the depth chart his rookie season in Cleveland.
46.outlook: If you like your quarterback big and athletic, then Taylen Green is worth a spot on your dynasty rosters. Green stands out in the Cleveland camp, listed at 6'6, 227 pounds, with speed that is elite for the quarterback position after clocking a 3.37 40-yard time at the combine. Green is as explosive as they come, posting a nearly perfect Relative Athletic Score. However, athleticism alone is not enough to push your way up the depth chart. While Green is destined to end up on a practice squad in 2026, early returns have been positive, as seen during OTAs and camp, with better-than-expected play from the pocket. Green has all the physical tools to get you excited, but needs time to refine his mechanics, fundamentals, and overall consistency. Coach Todd Monken spoke early in OTAs that he was impressed by Green's ability to learn and process, but also noted that to play on Sunday, Green had to work on footwork, cadence, and tightening that release.

47.name: Aidan O'Connell
47.comment: O'Connell got in the last game of the season, going 10-of-22 for 102 yards against the Chiefs. It was not an impressive showing at all. He missed nearly all the season after breaking his wrist in the preseason. O'Connell has 17 career starts and 20-passing touchdowns to 11 interceptions. He has played well at times but seems best suited for backup duty right now, a job he will try to win this season. O'Connell has good accuracy on shorter throws and does well in hitting his receivers in stride. He won't make many plays with his legs, though, and can struggle with his accuracy on deeper throws.
47.outlook: O'Connell has looked good at times when getting a chance to start but his ceiling isn't too high in a starting role. He might be worth a spot start but that is about it.

48.name: Cole Payton
48.comment: The Eagles took one of the best athletes in the entire draft, taking Payton in the fifth round of this year's draft. Payton could be used in a variety of ways his rookie season, similar to Taysom Hill. He has that kind of skill set. Payton has limited starting experience but does well on the short pass. He has a quick release. Payton can make plays on the run and is tough to bring down with the all in is hands in the open field. Payton will struggle some on the deeper throws and his inexperience is a concern at this stage of his career.
48.outlook: When you are fourth on the team's depth chart, the outlook for the season is not positive. In Philadelphia, the Eagles currently have Jalen Hurts, Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee, and rookie Cole Payton on the roster. While the Eagles could cut a veteran signal-caller, it is more likely they hope to sign Payton to their practice squad. The well-polished lefty completed 161 of 224 passes (71.8%) for 2,719 yards and 16 passing touchdowns while adding 777 rushing yards on 136 attempts, which led to 13 more scores. With Payton's ability to run and throw, it makes sense that the Eagles would want to keep him on the roster as a potential replacement for Jalen Hurts if he were to miss significant time in the future. Eagles scout, Duke Tobin, pounded the table for Payton, giving him his red star, calling him the toughest player on the team, and saying he's wired like an Eagle.

49.name: Anthony Richardson
49.comment: Richardson had a lost season. He was unable to win the starting job from Daniel Jones and ended up suffering a freak injury in a pregame workout, fracturing his orbital bone. He was eventually placed on Injured Reserve, missing most of the season. There is concern his eye injury could be an issue moving forward. And with his poor play recently, Richardson could be buried on the Colts depth chart as the No. 3 quarterback. At this point, a change of scenery might be best for Richardson. He has really struggled with accuracy and turnovers throughout his career. He completes just 50.6 percent of his passes and has 13 interceptions in 17 games (15 starts). Richardson is as athletic as any quarterback in the game, though. He has a great arm, can run like a running back, and make plays on the run as both a passer and runner. Richardson will miss on some passes he should make and forces some throws. Durability also is a concern after having injury issues to start his career.
49.outlook: Richardson has a huge ceiling if he starts because of his rushing ability. But his passing woes likely prevent him from starting unless injury hits. He is not worth a roster spot.

50.name: Gardner Minshew II
50.comment: Minshew was the top backup for the Chiefs last year and got a chance to start late in the year after Patrick Mahomes was injured. Minshew didn't last long in a starting role, though, hurting his knee. He was 3-of-8 for 15 yards in Week 16 before his injury. The good news is Minshew didn't suffer a serious injury and should be fine for the coming season. Minshew has plenty of starting experience and success in that role, but might be best suited as a backup at this stage of his career. His starting experience has been all over the map. He signed with the Cardinals and likely serves as their top backup this year. Minshew has 73 total touchdowns to just 34 interceptions in seven seasons. Minshew is a playmaker. He moves around the pocket well and makes most of his big plays outside the pocket. He does miss some throws he should make and his accuracy can be an issue. He also will force some passes he shouldn't attempt.
50.outlook: Minshew might be worth a look if he gets some starts. He is always capable of the big game based on his track record.

51.name: Spencer Rattler
51.comment: Rattler opened the season as the starter for the Saints before eventually giving way to rookie Tyler Shough, who ran with the job. Rattler had eight touchdowns to five interceptions in eight starts. He completed an impressive 67.7 percent of his passes. He was just 1-7 as the starter, though. And he had more than 20 fantasy points just one of those games. Shough is going to be the starter in New Orleans for years to come, putting Rattler in the backup role. He should fill that spot well. Rattler has a very strong arm and can be accurate. Rattler also does well in making plays on the run as a passer or runner. He will struggle some when pressured, though, and can force throws that aren't there.
51.outlook: Rattler got some starts once again last year but didn't help fantasy teams. So even if he gets a few more chances this year, don't expect much.

52.name: Drew Allar
52.comment: Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of this year's draft. He has the makeup to be a solid NFL starter. He has great size for the position and the arm to make all the throws. He can really fit the ball in tight windows because of his great arm. Allar struggled against good teams, though, accuracy can be an issue for him. He had a great 2024 season but struggled last year, causing him to fall way down draft boards. Allar is likely third on the depth chart his rookie year but lands in a good situation to eventually move into a starting role.
52.outlook: Some were surprised that the Pittsburgh Steelers made former Penn State quarterback Drew Allar a third-round pick in April's NFL Draft. However, general manager Omar Khan and head coach Mike McCarthy clearly believe Allar could be a long-term solution to the Steelers' franchise quarterback void. Though Allar's best moments in Happy Valley showcased a rocket arm and mobility for his "6-foot-5" frame, he certainly struggled with accuracy (63.2% completion) and efficiency (7.4 yards per attempt) over the course of a college career that featured 1,002 total pass attempts. Pittsburgh's plan became even more evident in May, when the team re-signed Aaron Rodgers to a one-year deal. Veteran quarterback Mason Rudolph and 2025 fifth-round pick Will Howard are also returning in 2026 to compete for the backup job. It seems that if the Steelers' season goes according to plan, Allar won't play any meaningful snaps in 2026. Pittsburgh has repeatedly said they're reworking his mechanics and "uninstalling" - a direct quote from McCarthy - everything he learned at Penn State. In redraft formats, that means Allar isn't worth any consideration as a draft selection, and dynasty managers will have to be patient with a player whose college career leaves an ambiguous forecast for his pro future.

53.name: Jameis Winston
53.comment: Winston was all over the depth chart for the Giants last year. He was second or third most of the year but also started two games. He had a huge showing Week 12, throwing for 366 yards and two touchdowns. Winston scored 36.9 fantasy points, showing his big-game potential once again. Winston has been a top backup in recent seasons and likely to serve that role once again this year. Winston has 4,000-plus yards three of 11 seasons. He also has 15 or more interceptions three seasons. Turnovers and decision making are an issue for Winston. He has a great arm and can make all the throws. Winston can struggle with accuracy at times, though, completing 61.1 percent of his passes for his career. Winston is a good athlete but more of a pocket passer than scrambler. He will make plays with his legs when needed.
53.outlook: Winston can be a top fantasy quarterback in a starting role. It is going to be hard for him to be a full-time starter because of his turnover and accuracy issues, though. So unless he is starting, don't bother.

54.name: Cade Klubnik
54.comment: The Jets used a fourth-round pick on Klubnik in this year's draft. New York is still looking for their franchise quarterback and hope that Klubnik might become that guy. He is a really good pocket passer that can make all the throws. Klubnik has good mechanics for the position. He is indecisive at times, though, and isn't always on time with his throws. Klubnik is a bit of a developmental player and likely third on the depth chart his rookie season in New York.
54.outlook: Klubnik lands in a good spot but might take some time to find the field. But if he progresses, good things could be in store for him down the road.  '

55.name: Tyler Huntley
55.comment: Huntley was the top backup for the Ravens last year and got in five games, starting two. He completed 77.6 percent of his passes and had two touchdowns without an interception. Huntley showed well with his chances. Huntley has shown some good things when given the chance, serving as a dual threat quarterback. He hopes to be a starter in the NFL at some point, but seems likely to be a top backup once again this year. Huntley needs work on his decision making, cutting down on the turnovers (10 career interceptions). He also doesn't take a ton of chances down the field, taking off as a runner probably sooner than he should. He has shown improvement in these areas, but still needs work.
55.outlook: Huntley is capable of being a spot fantasy starter when getting a chance to start. He is a dual threat with a decent weekly floor because of his rushing ability. The chances of Huntley starting are fairly slim, though.

56.name: Jake Browning
56.comment: Browning got three starts last year and played five games. He was unable to keep the starting job, though, giving way to Joe Flacco. Browning was erratic with his play, having two games with 20-plus fantasy points and two others with fewer than 10 points He had seven total touchdowns to eight interceptions. His up and down play likely leads him to another top back-up job this season. Browning signed with the Bucs this offseason to take over as their top backup. Browning is very accurate and gets rid of the ball quickly. He doesn't have a huge arm but it is strong enough to make all the throws. Browning can also make plays with his legs, having four rushing touchdowns for his career. Browning will force some passes, though, and can struggle a little on the deep ball. Turnovers have been an issue, having 15 interceptions in 17 games.
56.outlook: Browning has shown some potential when starting so if forced to start again, he might be worth a look in the right matchup.

57.name: Tanner McKee
57.comment: McKee was the top backup for the Eagles last year and got the start the last week of the season with the Eagles resting their starters. He played pretty well, going 21-of-40 for 241 yards and a touchdown with an interception. McKee has played well with his limited chances in two seasons. He has five touchdowns to one interception. He should be the top backup for the Eagles once again this season but has some promise to be a starter at some point in his career. McKee is a big quarterback with a strong arm. He has a few accuracy issues and can struggle with turnovers.
57.outlook: McKee might be worth grabbing if Jalen Hurts gets hurt. He has some potential in this offense.

58.name: Mason Rudolph
58.comment: Rudolph was back with the Steelers last year to serve as their top backup. He got in five games and even got a start. Rudolph was 38-of-52 for 310 yard and two touchdowns with two interceptions. He didn't do much in his only start, getting 11.25 fantasy points in Week 12 against the Bears. Rudolph has started some games throughout his career but never really excelled when given the chance. He serves the backup role well, though, and should continue in that role going forward. Rudolph is a big quarterback that can make all the throws. He has very good touch but also can fit the ball into tight spaces if needed. He does lack a little arm strength, though, and struggles some with the deep ball. Rudolph also has issues when being pressured, making some poor decisions under duress.
58.outlook: Rudolph shows some potential when starting but has never been much of a help to fantasy teams. So even if he starts some games, he will be a stretch for fantasy teams.

59.name: Tyrod Taylor
59.comment: Taylor got some chances to serve as the Jets starter last year but was unable to keep that job. He had some good games but struggled in others. He started four games and played in six. He complete just 59.7 percent of his passes and had six total touchdowns to five interceptions. Taylor had two games with 20-plus fantasy points. Taylor is likely headed to his usual backup role this season, a role he can serve well. Taylor has two seasons with more than 3,000-passing yards as the starter for the Bills. He also has run for more than 400 yards three seasons as the starter for Buffalo. Taylor has a very strong arm and throws a good deep ball. He will struggle with accuracy and still holds onto the ball too long. He doesn't force many passes and will make plays with his legs when given a chance. Taylor is indecisive with his passes and tends to stall in the red zone.
59.outlook: Taylor has some value as a starting quarterback because of his ability to make plays with his legs. But until he is in the starting lineup, don't bother with him on your roster. And even if he starts, expect erratic numbers.

61.name: Joe Milton III
61.comment: Milton got in four games his first season as the Cowboys top backup quarterback. He was 15-of-24 for 183 yards and a touchdown with an interception. He should continue to be the No. 2 for Dallas. And Milton could be the future for the Cowboys, playing behind Prescott for a few seasons before taking over as the starter. Milton has a huge arm. It is as good as any quarterback in all of football. He can make plays on the move but isn't much of a rushing quarterback. He can force some passes and struggle with consistency, relying on his big arm too much.
61.outlook: Milton is not draft material but if Prescott gets hurt, he would be a really intriguing weekly play as a starter.

62.name: Davis Mills
62.comment: Mills was the top backup for the Texans once again. He started three games because of injury and didn't lose any of those games. He had five touchdowns to an interception for the season. He scored 31.6 fantasy points in Week 10 against the Jaguars. Mills does well in a backup role and should fill that again this season. Mills has a great arm and can make all the throws. He gets rid of the ball in a hurry and his arm can be a difference maker in the passing game. He does tend to hold onto the ball too long and will make bad decisions when pressured. Mills will force passes. He led the league in interceptions in 2022 and has 26 interceptions in five seasons.
62.outlook: Mills has looked decent at times but is no sure thing if forced to start. He was good for fantasy teams in just one of his three starts last year.

63.name: Trey Lance
63.comment: Lance was the top backup for the Cowboys last year and got to start the last game of the season. He didn't do much in that start, though, going 20-of-44 for just 136 yards. He did run for 69 yards, though, showing his ability to make plays with his legs. Lance seems destined for backup duty once again this year. Lance has big-time ability at the position. Lance is a playmaker - making plays with his arm and legs. Lance has a great arm and can make all the throws. He also is a very good runner. Lance lacks accuracy, though, and remains raw. He has done very little to date when given the chance to play.
63.outlook: Lance would be an intriguing fantasy play if he happens to get some starts but that seems a long shot at this point. Until he is starting, don't bother.

64.name: Mitchell Trubisky
64.comment: Trubisky was the top backup for the Bills last season for the second straight year. He got in four games, going 25-of-35 for 313 yards and four touchdowns without an interceptions. He played nearly the entire last game of the year and played really well. He scored 31.45 fantasy points against the Jets. Trubisky will be the top backup for the Titans this year, playing behind Cam Ward. He has 57 career starts and some success in that role. Trubisky still tends to lock on a receiver and make the wrong read. He is a good athlete with decent height and strength. He isn't a running quarterback but can make plays with his legs. Trubisky has a solid arm that can make all the throws. He still needs work on his decision making while limiting turnovers.
64.outlook: Trubisky was not a help to fantasy teams while starting in past years. He is not likely to help fantasy teams this year, even if he finds his way into the starting lineup once again.

65.name: Carson Wentz
65.comment: Wentz found his way into the starting lineup for the Vikings last year but had his season cut short because of a shoulder injury. He was hurt in Week 8 and needed surgery for the injury, missing the rest of the year. He played alright in his five starts. Wentz completed 65 percent of his passes and had six touchdowns to five interceptions. He had one game with 20-plus fantasy points. Wentz probably proved he remains more of a backup at this stage of his career, a role he should serve with the Vikings. He has not exactly seized his opportunities to start the last few years. Wentz is a big quarterback with a plus arm but also has the athletic ability to make plays with his legs. He normally limits turnovers and completes a high percentage of his passes but has struggled some in both areas the last few seasons, seeing his play take a step backwards. Injuries are always a concern for Wentz, playing a full season just three times when in a starting role.
65.outlook: Wentz is erratic when starting, making him a tough fantasy player to trust. He might be worth a spot start in the right matchup if forced into a starting role once again.

66.name: Jimmy Garoppolo
66.comment: Garoppolo was the top backup for the Rams for a second straight season. He got in three games and didn't attempt a pass. Garoppolo serves the backup role very well and should continue to serve that role going forward. Garoppolo has a very quick release and a good arm. He is accurate on underneath throws but will struggle some on deeper throws. Garoppolo isn't the biggest quarterback, so durability is always a concern for him, especially if you consider he has endured injury issues throughout his career. Garoppolo also struggles some when being forced to make the big play.
66.outlook: Garoppolo might be worth a look if he starts once again and shows something on the field. It has happened in the past, but we just aren't sure it happens once again.

67.name: Joshua Dobbs
67.comment: Dobbs was the top backup for the Patriots last year and got in four games in that role. He was 7-of-10 for 70 yards. He failed to start a game for the first item since 2021. Dobbs has shown pretty well at times in recent years when getting a chance to start, giving him good value as a top NFL backup. He will continue to serve that role this year. Dobbs is an athletic quarterback that has a knack for making plays. He throws a very good deep ball and does a good job of going through his progressions to make the correct choice. Dobbs has a bit of a slow delivery and can be inaccurate at times.
67.outlook: If he finds his way onto the field, Dobbs is worth a look for fantasy teams. He has some big-game potential.

68.name: Will Levis
68.comment: Levis missed all of last season because of a shoulder injury, which required surgery. He should be ready for the start of camp and the coming season. He will move to a backup role for the Titans, playing behind Cam Ward. Levis is plenty young enough to still turn his career around but might need to learn in a backup role for a few season before getting his chance again. Levis needs to improve his accuracy and decision making if he hopes to start. Levis has great size for the position. He is very athletic and has a top arm. He can make all the throws. He also isn't afraid to make plays with his legs. Levis has some accuracy issues, though, and turnovers are an issue. He remains a work in progress.
68.outlook: Levis has no fantasy value this year but could down the road if he ever gets another shot to start. There is some potential there.

69.name: Kenny Pickett
69.comment: Pickett was third on the depth chart last year for the Raiders but did get a start in Week 15 against the Eagles. He really struggled in that game, going 15-of-25 for just 64 yards with an interception. Pickett can do well in the top backup role, though, and will look to earn that job this season with the Panthers. He has 16 interceptions to 16-passing touchdowns in four seasons. Pickett is a pretty accurate, pocket passer that does a good job of reading defenses and making plays. He lacks a huge arm compared to some of the other quarterbacks in the league, though. He is not afraid to make plays with his legs but isn't near the level of other rushing quarterbacks. Pickett will force some throws and turns the ball over too much at this stage of his career.
69.outlook: Pickett has shown little to date for fantasy teams so even if he happens to find his way into the starting lineup once again, he probably won't be a huge help.

70.name: Drew Lock
70.comment: Lock returned to the Seahawks last year and was their top backup behind Sam Darnold. Lock got in five games, going 2-of-3 for 15 yards. Lock has gotten chances to start in the past but hasn't excelled in that role. He is looking more and more like a top NFL backup, a role he can serve well. Lock has a huge arm and can make all the throws. He will make some plays with his legs, using his athletic ability. He will miss some easy throws and can struggle with mechanics at times because of his great arm, trusting his arm strength more so than having proper technique. He also is indecisive in the pocket. Lock has not progressed as expected and might have a hard time being a full-time starter in the NFL.
70.outlook: Lock s a big stretch to use even if he finds his way into the starting lineup once again. He has been little help to fantasy teams to date.

71.name: Jalen Milroe
71.comment: Milroe was third on the Seahawks depth chart his rookie season. He did get in a few games but didn't attempt a pass. Milroe will look to move up the depth chart this year and claim the top backup job to Sam Darnold. Milroe could be the starter for the Seahawks down the road but likely will have to learn a few seasons before getting his shot. Milroe is not the most accurate passer. He will struggle with some of his throws but shows flashes of big-time things when all is going well for him. His biggest asset is as a runner right now. He has game-changing speed and can make a some huge plays with his legs. He will really need to improve as a thrower to be a starter in the NFL.
71.outlook: Milroe has a huge ceiling if playing because of his rushing ability. But he is not expected to see the field this season with Sam Darnold as the starter right now.

72.name: Case Keenum
72.comment: Keenum was third on the depth chart for the Bears last season and didn't get in a game. He was inactive most weeks. Keenum has not played in an NFL game since 2023. Keenum does well as a NFL backup and will look to earn that role once again this year. Keenum has two seasons with 3,500-plus passing yards and 20-plus touchdowns. Keenum moves around the pocket pretty well and has a good arm. He had some accuracy issues earlier in his career, but really made strides in that area in recent seasons. He plays very well outside of the pocket and throws a much-improved deep ball. He forces some throws, though, and doesn't do a great job of taking care of the ball.
72.outlook: Keenum can be worth some spot starts when he is starting. He has some big-game ability and success when starting.

73.name: Desmond Ridder
73.comment: Ridder bounced around the league last year, eventually signing with the Packers late in the season to serve as the second or third quarterback with Jordan Love banged up. Ridder didn't play a game in that role. Ridder has not progressed as expected and is just fighting for his NFL life. He will look to earn a backup role this season. He has 16-passing touchdowns to 14 interceptions for his career, having 18 career starts. Ridder is a very good athlete. He can make plays with his arm and legs. Ridder lacks a little arm strength, though, and will struggle some on accuracy with the deep ball. And his decision making has been a problem in a starting role, leading to too many turnovers.
73.outlook: Ridder has a little big-game potential but is a stretch for fantasy teams to use if he happens to get a few more starts this season.

74.name: Cooper Rush
74.comment: Rush played his first season with the Ravens last year and was second or third on the depth chart throughout the season. He started two games and struggled, having four interceptions without a score. He didn't even top six fantasy points in ether start. His poor play led to the Ravens looking in another direction with Lamar Jackson out. Rush is going to need to pick up his play if he hopes to earn a top backup job this season. Rush does not have an NFL arm but can be accurate and do well on shorter throws. He is not much of a runner and more of a pocket passer. He will not take a lot of chances down the field.
74.outlook: Rush is a big risk to use - even if he happens to get some starts. He was a mess last year.

75.name: Zach Wilson
75.comment: Wilson got in four games last year, going 6-of-11 for 32 yards without a touchdown or an interception. He was the top backup much of the year but when the Dolphins made a change at quarterback, he didn't get a chance to start, which should tell you something about what the team thinks of him. Wilson has fallen a long way since being a first-round pick. He seems destined for backup duty. In 33 career starts, Wilson has 23 touchdown passes compared to 25 interceptions and completes 57 percent of his passes. Wilson is a big-time talent at the position. He has a great arm and can make some amazing throws, especially on the run. He throws a great deep ball and does well on the run. His decision making and accuracy are a mess at this stage of his career. Wilson also will make poor choices when under pressure.
75.outlook: Wilson has been little help to fantasy teams even when starting and seems a long shot to take much of a step forward this year.

76.name: Tyson Bagent
76.comment: Bagent was the top backup for the Bears for a third straight season. He was 3-of-4 for 47 yards in three games. He has not started a game since his rookie season. Bagent seems stuck in a reserve role for the Bears as long as Caleb Williams is around. He serves the role well, though. Bagent is an accurate quarterback with a strong arm. He also moves around the pocket well and can make plays with his legs as a runner. Bagent continues to make big strides each offseason and will look to take another step forward this year.
76.outlook: Bagent could be a starter in the NFL at some point, but that is not going to come this year unless injury hits. But if that happens, he is worth grabbing to see what he can do with more chances.

77.name: Will Howard
77.comment: Howard was third on the Steelers depth chart his rookie season. He did not attempt a pass. He will look to move up the depth chart this year and play a bigger role with the team. Howard does well in hitting his receivers in stride and extending the play. He will lack some accuracy at times, though, and his arm is just alright. Howard can make some plays with his legs if needed.
77.outlook: Howard is more intriguing in dynasty formats. He could move up the depth chart and eventually get a chance with the Steelers. But for now, he is not worth a draft pick.

78.name: Clayton Tune
78.comment: Tune was third string for the Packers for much of last season. He got in two games, going 7-of-15 for 42 yards with an interception. Tune has started two NFL games but not shown a whole lot in those starts. He will look to earn a top backup job this season. Tune is more of a pocket passer. He has a decent arm and can do well in the pocket. He lacks a little pocket awareness, though, and will make few plays with his legs as either a passer or runner. He can struggle some when pressured and has yet to do much with past chances in the NFL.
78.outlook: Tune would be a stretch to use for fantasy teams even if he happens to get some playing time.

79.name: Garrett Nussmeier
79.comment: A poor senior season and injury issues saw Nussmeier fall much further than expected in this year's draft. The Chiefs took him in the seventh round. He lands in a good spot to learn, though, getting a chance to watch Patrick Mahomes. Nussmeier is likely third on the depth chart his rookie year. He has a great arm and can make plays on the run. He does well in hitting his receivers in stride. His decision making can be a big issue, forcing throws.
79.outlook: Nussmeier is not going to help fantasy teams right now. He might in a few years.

80.name: Brett Rypien
80.comment: Rypien was with the Bengals and Colts last year, serving a backup role with both teams. He did not attempt a pass. Rypien has been on five teams since 2022. Rypien has gotten some starts in recent years, but not done much with those. Rypien is destined for backup duty once again, trying to win a top backup job. Rypien has a pretty good arm and can make some plays down the field. He is not afraid to take some chances. He lacks a little accuracy, though, and can struggle with decision making when pressured.
80.outlook: Rypien has played some in recent seasons but done little for fantasy teams in a starting role. He is not a player to target and could struggle when pressed into a starting role.

81.name: Mike White
81.comment: White did not get in a game last year. He was on the Panthers practice squad much of the season. White will look to earn a top backup job this year, a role he can serve well. He has some starting experience and showed some promise when on the field. White has a good arm and isn't afraid to take chances down the field. He is an accurate quarterback with a quick release. White can be careless with the football, though, and take unnecessary risks.
81.outlook: White has made plays when given a chance to start, so if that happens again, he might be worth a wavier-wire add. He is capable of the big game.

82.name: Hendon Hooker
82.comment: Hooker bounced around last year after failing to win the top backup job in Detroit. He was on the Panthers and Jets rosters but unable to get in a game. He is hoping to win a backup job this coming season but nothing is certain. Hooker has attempted nine passes for his career. Hooker gets rid of the ball quickly and normally makes the right reads. He has a solid arm and is not afraid to make plays with his legs. He remains raw, though, and doesn't have a lot of experience just yet playing in a pro-style offense.
82.outlook: Hooker is trending the wrong way. Pass.

83.name: Tommy DeVito
83.comment: DeVito was unable to keep a roster spot with the Giants before last year but was claimed by the Patriots. He was third on their depth chart and failed to get in a game. He will look to move up the depth chart this year and serve as the top backup. DeVito is a playmaker. He will miss on some throws he should make, but seems to make key plays at the right time. DeVito has a decent arm and can be accurate. He doesn't take a ton of chances and doesn't always make the right reads.
83.outlook: DeVito seems a long shot to find the field this year.

84.name: Nick Mullens
84.comment: Mullens played with the Jaguars last year, serving as the top backup to Trevor Lawrence. Mullens got some playing time in mop-up duty, going 3-of-3 for 19 yards in five games. Mullens can serve the backup role well. He has some success in a starting role and can help in a pinch. Mullens has a strong arm and quick release. He reads defenses pretty well and does a good job of making the big play. He will force passes, though, and doesn't always make the right decisions.
84.outlook: Mullens has plenty of fantasy potential when starting. Just expect some turnovers to go with those yardage and touchdown totals.

85.name: Skylar Thompson
85.comment: Thompson was the third string quarterback for the Steelers last year but spent nearly the entire season on Injured Reserve because of a hamstring injury. Thompson started his career with the Dolphins and has three career starts. He hasn't shown a lot in a starting role but at least has some NFL experience. He will look to move up the depth chart this year and serve as a top backup. Thompson has a solid arm and can make all the throws. He won't take many chances down the field, though, and looks indecisive in the pocket.
85.outlook: Thompson hasn't shown a whole lot while on the field. He is young, though, so he isn't a total lost cause just yet.

86.name: Sam Howell
86.comment: Howell was with the Eagles last year and served as the No. 3 in his first year with the team. Howell had some success in a starting role for the Commanders a few seasons back, so he could work his way back into a starting lineup at some point. But for now, he seems destined for backup duty. Howell is a playmaker at the position. He does well in improvising and making plays from all over the pocket. His accuracy can be an issues a times, especially on the deep ball. He also can be careless with the football, leading to too many turnovers.
86.outlook: Howell showed he can help fantasy teams when starting, but nothing is certain at this point. If he starts again, Howell is a legit spot starter for fantasy teams. He can post the big game.

87.name: Easton Stick
87.comment: Stick was third on the depth chart for the Falcons most of last season. He didn't get in a game. Stick has started four games during his career and done alight with those chances. He will look to earn a top backup job this season. Stick is an accurate quarterback that does well on the move. He is good at moving around the pocket and making plays with his arm or legs. He also is a good downfield thrower with a strong arm. He does tend to try to use his legs too often, abandoning the progressions in the passing game too quickly.
87.outlook: Stick will get his rushing yards, so he has some potential if finding his way into the starting lineup. He might be worth a spot start in a pinch, but the chances of him starting seem very slim.

88.name: Kyle Allen
88.comment: Allen was the top backup for the Lions last year, attempting two passes in three games. He has been a top backup for four different teams in four years. He serves the role well, though. Allen has started 19 games in his career and played alright when given the chance. Allen is a pretty good athlete with a solid arm that normally makes sound decisions. He is a pretty accurate quarterback. Allen will force some passes, though, and doesn't always make the right reads.
88.outlook: Allen has never been much of a help to fantasy teams when given the chance to start, so he will be a reach for fantasy teams even if he manages to find the field this season.

89.name: Jarrett Stidham
89.comment: Stidham was the top backup for the Broncos once again last year but didn't attempt a pass until the playoffs. He started the AFC Championship game after Bo Nix was injured the previous week. Stidham played decent in the big game, going 17-of-31 for 133 yards and a touchdown with an interception. Stidham has started four regular season games during his career, going 1-3 in those games. At this point, Stidham doesn't seem likely to earn a starting job. He seems destined for backup duty, a role he serves well. Stidham is a good athlete with a great arm. He has a pro arm and the athleticism to make plays. He has accuracy issues, though, and can struggle under pressure. He will make poor decisions when pressured.
89.outlook: Stidham has been pretty ho hum when starting, so he seems to have little fantasy value even if given more chances to start.

90.name: C.J. Beathard
90.comment: Beathard was on the Lions practice squad all of last year and didn't play a game. He has failed to play a game two straight seasons. Beathard will try to earn a top backup job this year. He is capable, having starting experience and some past success. Beathard has a solid arm and just a knack for making plays. He lacks some accuracy, though, and will force some throws. He can make plays with his legs if a play breaks down.
90.outlook: Beathard has not produced very good fantasy numbers with past chances, so even if he gets a few starts, his fantasy value is limited.

91.name: Stetson Bennett
91.comment: Bennett was third on the Rams depth chart once again last season and did not get in a game in that role. He will look to move up the depth chart this year and serve as the top backup for the team. Bennett is yet to attempt a pass in the NFL. Bennett lacks size and arm strength, but places the ball well and plays with a swagger. He also can make plays on the move. He will struggle come with deeper throw and his lack of arm strength for the pro game is a concern.
91.outlook: Bennett could be worth a look if he happens to find the field in this offense, but the chances of him playing seem pretty slim at this point.

92.name: Bailey Zappe
92.comment: Zappe was on the Browns practice squad last season. Zappe continues to trend the wrong way since getting some stars with the Patriots his first two seasons in the NFL. He has nine starts in four seasons in the NFL. He is best suited to be a backup than starter, though, a role he should compete for this year. Zappe is a pocket passer. He has good touch on the ball and can make all the throws from the pocket. He lacks a little size for the position, though, and doesn't have a huge arm. His lack of arm strength can cause issues on fitting the ball in tight windows. He also will force some throws and turnovers have been an issues for him since entering the league.
92.outlook: Zappe is a big risk to use if getting a chance to start. He is turnover prone and lacks accuracy.

93.name: Behren Morton
93.comment: New England selected Morton in the seventh round of this year's draft. He will look to become the top backup to Drake Maye but might take a year or two to reach that role. Morton has a quick release and is a very accurate passer. He does well in working through his progressions and picking the right target.
93.outlook: Morton is a little intriguing if he happens to find the field but is a big-time long shot to play his rookie year.

94.name: Sean Clifford
94.comment: Clifford was on the Bengals practice squad most of last season. He will look to earn a top backup job this year but nothing is certain. Clifford does well in making plays with his legs. He can be a dual threat. He doesn't have a great arm, though, and lacks accuracy. He can be late on his throws.
94.outlook: Clifford can make some plays with his legs, so he has a little fantasy value if he finds the field. But he seems a real long shot to play.

95.name: Kyle McCord
95.comment: McCord was on the Eagles practice squad his rookie season. He signed with the Packers after the season and will look to earn a backup job with his new team. McCord is a solid pocket passer that spreads the ball around well. He led college football in passing yards his last year in college. His arm strength is just alright and he has a tendency to lock on a receiver.
95.outlook: McCord is a long shot to find the field. He is just hoping to earn a roster spot.

96.name: Athan Kaliakmanis
96.comment: The Commanders took Kaliakmanis in the seventh round of this year's draft. He will try to earn a roster spot as the No. 3 quarterback for the team. He looks the part at the position. He has a solid arm and improved accuracy throughout his college career. He is not very mobile in the pocket, though, and will make few plays with his legs.
96.outlook: Kaliakmanis is going to be low on the depth chart his rookie year. Don't bother.

97.name: Chris Oladokun
97.comment: Oladokun was third on the the Chiefs depth chart last year but found his way into the starting lineup at the end of the season because of injuries. He started two games but failed to top 120-passing yards in either game and had a touchdown. The one positive was he showed decent accuracy, completing 63.6 percent of his passes. He will look to be the top backup for the Chiefs this year but could be stuck as the No. 3. Oladokun is a fairly accurate quarterback that can make some plays with his legs. He will struggle to push the ball down the field, though, and takes few chances.
97.outlook: Oladokun was a terrible fantasy play in a starting role last year. He would be a big stretch for fantasy teams to use if he happened to start again this year.

98.name: Cam Miller
98.comment: Miller was on the Raiders practice squad his rookie season. He signed with the Dolphins after the season and will look to earn a backup job with his new team this season. Miller is not a big player but does well in the pocket and making throws under duress. Miller gets the football out quick and hits his receivers in stride. He lacks some size for the position and his arm is just adequate.
98.outlook: Miller would be a surprise to find the field.

99.name: Graham Mertz
99.comment: Mertz was the No. 3 quarterback for the Texans his rookie season. He did not get in a game. Mertz will look to move up the depth chart in Houston and earn that top backup job. Mertz is an accurate quarterback that normally makes good decisions. Health is a huge concern for him after battling injuries throughout much of his college career.
99.outlook: Mertz is going to have a hard time finding the field. Don't bother.

100.name: Brady Cook
100.comment: Cook was an undrafted free agent but was signed by the Jets to be their No. 3 quarterback. He was their surprise starter late in the season with the team all banged up at quarterback. Cook got some chances and showed he needs plenty of seasoning. Cook had two touchdowns to seven interceptions in five games (four starts). He completed just 57.5 percent of his passes. He really struggled with is accuracy, having an on-target percentage of just 67.8 percent. Cook will look to win the top backup job for the Jets this year but nothing is certain. He has some potential, though. Cook has a pretty strong arm and a quick release. He moves around the pocket well and will make plays with his legs when needed. His accuracy can be an issue on the deep ball and he will make some poor decisions when pressured.
100.outlook: It is hard to fault Cook too much for last year. He had next to nothing to work with when starting. But even with that said, he would be a stretch for fantasy teams to use if forced into a starting role again this year.
